97	/** Sources `worker/game-mods.ts` can resolve to a downloadable file. */
98	export const RESOLVABLE_SOURCES = new Set([
99	  "modrinth",
100	  "spigotmc",
101	  "umod",
102	  "thunderstore",
103	  "github",
104	  // Not a "downloadable file" in the same sense as the others — see the big
105	  // comment above INSTALLABLE_FAMILIES's Workshop entries — but it has to be
106	  // in this set too: `installSupport()` below requires BOTH the family and
107	  // the source to be listed before it will draw an Install button at all.
108	  "steam_workshop",
109	]);
110	// "github" added 2026-09-20 alongside scripts/import-github-catalog.ts (real CS2
111	// plugin catalogue). Resolving works today (worker/game-mods.ts's resolveUrl
112	// hits the repo's real `/releases/latest` asset) but no family in
113	// INSTALLABLE_FAMILIES below is github-sourced yet — cs2 mods still show
114	// installSupport's "family" reason (INSTALLABLE_FAMILIES has no cs2 entry:
115	// nobody has written the real SSH mod-directory convention for a CS2 dedicated
116	// server yet, see modDirShell's TODO in worker/game-mods.ts). Wiring
117	// RESOLVABLE_SOURCES ahead of INSTALLABLE_FAMILIES is deliberate: it makes the
118	// panel's error message correctly blame the game ("not wired for this game
119	// yet") instead of the source, and it means the day someone adds a `cs2` case
120	// to modDirShell, install just works with no further changes here.
121	
122	export type InstallSupport =
123	  | { ok: true }
124	  | { ok: false; reason: "family" | "source"; message: string };
125	
126	/**
127	 * Can this entry be installed for the customer, or does it have to be done by
128	 * hand? The message is customer-facing and says which of the two is missing,
129	 * because they lead to different next steps: a family we can't reach means
130	 * upload it yourself, a source we can't fetch from means download it first.
131	 */
132	export function installSupport(family: string, source: string): InstallSupport {
133	  if (!INSTALLABLE_FAMILIES.has(family)) {
134	    return {
135	      ok: false,
136	      reason: "family",
137	      message: "We can't place files for this game automatically yet — install it yourself in Files.",
138	    };
139	  }
140	  if (!RESOLVABLE_SOURCES.has(source)) {
141	    return {
142	      ok: false,
143	      reason: "source",
144	      message: "This source doesn't offer a direct download we can fetch — grab the file and upload it in Files.",
145	    };
146	  }
147	  return { ok: true };
148	}

343	 * prefers that one, because "a TCP handshake is verifiable with a plain connect,
344	 * and the process binding it is proof the game server itself came up" — see its
345	 * own comment. For most families that port is also the join port, so the
346	 * distinction never mattered. For the eight below it is an RCON/query/admin
347	 * port, and `GAME_PORT`'s own inline comments have always said so.

350	 * own port" for NAT servers using this same map. Found live 2026-09-06 by
351	 * provisioning a real Rust server on node-2: the guest listened correctly on
352	 * 28015/udp (join) and 28016/tcp (RCON), the node's NAT had exactly one game
353	 * rule — 28016/tcp — and the dashboard handed the customer that RCON port as
354	 * their connect address. No player could ever have joined. That is the identical
355	 * outage found on the real paying customer `rust-w75hko` (see
356	 * docs/DOCUMENTATION.md's node migration section), whose root cause was
357	 * previously read as "allocateGameForward was never called for it"; it is called,
358	 * just with the wrong port.

361	 * prisma/catalog.ts / the seed-wave*-games.ts files — the only ports docker

364	 * `GAME_PORT` entry; use {@link joinPortFor} rather than reading this directly.

422	 * the ones in `GAME_JOIN_PORT_OVERRIDE`.

426	}

430	 * forwarded to actually be joinable — not more admin/RCON exposure, genuine
431	 * extra game-protocol ports. Found live 2026-09-08: Valheim's dedicated
432	 * server opens THREE consecutive UDP ports for its Steam networking layer
433	 * (base + query + a third), confirmed live against a real customer server —
434	 * with only the base port (2456) forwarded, the client got a hard "Failed to
435	 * connect" before ever reaching a password prompt. `worker/index.ts`'s NAT
436	 * auto-forward only ever created one PortForward row per server before this,
437	 * so every NAT Valheim order needed the customer to manually discover and add
438	 * the missing two — exactly the mistake that produced that ticket.
439	 *
440	 * Sourced from each family's own `docker run -p ...` mapping (prisma/
441	 * catalog.ts / seed-wave*-games.ts), same provenance discipline as
442	 * `GAME_JOIN_PORT_OVERRIDE` above — never guessed.
443	 *
444	 * Extended 2026-09-24 with 7 more families flagged by that audit as
445	 * "probably-unjoinable NAT servers" — each verified against the game's own
446	 * official docs/wiki (not guessed; see the per-entry citation below and the
447	 * research working notes referenced from lib/game-control.ts). Two corrections
448	 * the research turned up vs. the audit's own hypothesis, worth recording:
449	 *  - Sons of the Forest's real GamePort is 8766 (matches the existing
450	 *    GAME_PORT entry) — NOT 9700 as guessed; the two EXTRA ports are 27016
451	 *    (QueryPort) and 9700 (BlobSyncPort), confirmed against the community
452	 *    dedicated-server config field names AND that the server self-checks all
453	 *    three and refuses to start if any is unreachable.
454	 *  - ARK's 7778/udp is real but its official wiki frames it as Steam P2P
455	 *    advertising ("in-game browser advertising"), not a hard join requirement
456	 *    — forwarded anyway (defensible, zero cost, matches what most hosts do)
457	 *    but flagged medium-confidence rather than proven-required like the rest.
458	 *
459	 * DELIBERATELY INCOMPLETE: gmod/unturned/factorio (27015-27017 range) and eco/
460	 * empyrion/stationeers (27015-27016 or 30000-30003 ranges) still publish more
461	 * than their single joinPortFor() port and have NOT been individually verified
462	 * — not added here without that same live/documented verification first (a
463	 * wrong guess here creates the same class of bug this table exists to fix).
464	 */

469	  ],

471	  // that BOTH connection_dedicated_port and query_dedicated_port need BOTH
472	  // TCP and UDP rules forwarded ("For port forwarding both TPP/IP and UPD
473	  // rules are required" — sic, their own typo), not just the single UDP join
474	  // port most families need. GAME_PORT's 27015/udp is the primary join port
475	  // (already included by joinPortFor); these 3 are the remaining combos:
476	  // 27015/tcp, plus the query port (27016 default) on both protocols.
477	  ets2: [
478	    { port: 27015, protocol: "tcp" },
479	    { port: 27016, protocol: "udp" },
480	    { port: 27016, protocol: "tcp" },
481	  ],
482	  ats: [
483	    { port: 27015, protocol: "tcp" },
484	    { port: 27016, protocol: "udp" },
485	    { port: 27016, protocol: "tcp" },
486	  ],

488	  // "Port 8888 (TCP): Game traffic, Reliable messaging" — "If you have not
489	  // correctly forwarded the reliable messaging port, players can initiate a
490	  // connection but will be perpetually stuck on the 'loading' screen." Both
491	  // 7777/tcp and 7777/udp are published by the image; the wiki does not split
492	  // them the way Funcom does for Conan, so both stay forwarded alongside the
493	  // required 8888/tcp.
494	  satisfactory: [
495	    { port: 7777, protocol: "udp" },
496	    { port: 8888, protocol: "tcp" },
497	  ],

499	  // 10000/tcp is the "Queue Port", used whenever the server's queue system is
500	  // enabled (commonly on by default) so a player waiting for a full server can
501	  // actually hold their place — part of the real join path, not cosmetic.
502	  theisle: [{ port: 10000, protocol: "tcp" }],
503	  // Sons of the Forest — Endnight's own dedicated-server config field names
504	  // (GamePort=8766, QueryPort=27016, BlobSyncPort=9700), cross-verified
505	  // against the Steam Community dedicated-server guide, 2026-09-24: the

13851	### Task 3 — mod install: a real, generic mechanism already exists for 12 families; Terraria has two independent, genuine blockers
13852	
13853	`lib/mod-install-support.ts`'s `installSupport()` is the real gate behind "We can't place files for this game automatically yet" — and it turns out a real, working, generic download→place→restart mechanism (`worker/game-mods.ts`) already exists and is wired for **12 families**: minecraft, rust, valheim (via `modrinth`/`spigotmc`/`umod`/`thunderstore`, a direct SFTP `curl`-into-directory), plus ark, unturned, dst, squad, soulmask, projectzomboid, tf2, l4d2, empyrion (via Steam Workshop — a completely different, elegant mechanism: the worker writes the Workshop item id into whichever env var/config file the family's own dedicated-server binary already reads on boot, and the GAME ITSELF fetches the content from Steam; Nxeon never downloads or mirrors the file). This is real, live-gated behind `ENABLE_REAL_GAMEMODS` (set to `1` in production), not a stub.
13854	
13855	**Terraria is not wired, for two independent, genuine, and confirmed reasons — not because nobody got to it:**
13856	
13857	1. **The seeded catalog is the wrong platform for what Nxeon actually runs.** All 1000 seeded `GameMod` rows for `terraria` are `source: "steam_workshop"` — real content, but it's tModLoader's Workshop catalogue (tModLoader ships as its own separate Steam app; 1.4+ tModLoader mods are distributed through Steam Workshop under tModLoader's own listing, not Terraria's). Nxeon's actual Terraria product (`prisma/catalog.ts`'s `terraria` OsTemplate) runs `ryshe/terraria` — **vanilla Terraria + TShock, tModLoader is never installed.** There is no process on the server that would ever read a Workshop mod id or load a `.tmod` file. Auto-downloading one of these 1000 items would produce an inert file sitting unused — a fake "installed" state. A real fix means offering a second, tModLoader-based Terraria server variant; that's a product decision, not a mechanical wiring job, and out of scope here.
13858	2. **Even for the content type Nxeon's real Terraria server CAN use** — TShock plugins, genuine `.dll` files typically distributed as GitHub release assets (which the already-built `"github"` `RESOLVABLE_SOURCES` entry can fetch) — **there is nowhere to put one.** TShock installs at `/tshock` inside the `ryshe/terraria` container (confirmed via the image's own `/tshock/bootstrap.sh`, already cited in `prisma/catalog.ts`'s own comment for an earlier fix), and the template's only bind mount is `-v /opt/terraria:/root/.local/share/Terraria/Worlds` — the world-save folder. `/tshock/ServerPlugins` is not reachable from the host at all today. This means **neither an automated installer nor a customer's own manual "upload it in Files" can actually reach TShock's real plugin folder right now** — the honest fallback message is directionally correct but slightly understates the gap (it isn't just "not automated yet," it's "not reachable yet, automated or not").
13859	
13860	A real fix for reason 2 (bind-mount `/tshock/ServerPlugins` to a new host path in `prisma/catalog.ts`'s setupScript, add a `terraria` case to `worker/game-mods.ts`'s `modDirShell`, add `"terraria"` to `INSTALLABLE_FAMILIES`, and reseed the catalog with real TShock plugins instead of tModLoader Workshop items) is genuinely buildable and was fully scoped out — but was **not shipped this pass**, because a Docker bind mount over a path the image populates at build time can silently blank out whatever the image put there, and that must be verified against a real running container before it ships to a real product's provisioning script; it is not safe to ship blind. As documented under Bug 2 above, this session hit an explicit, repeated platform/permission boundary against provisioning new real test hardware (staging's sandbox flag, and a production workaround), so that live verification could not be done. Shipping an unverified infrastructure change to `prisma/catalog.ts` risks a real regression for every future Terraria order — worse than leaving today's honest gate in place. **Documented the full reasoning directly in `lib/mod-install-support.ts` (a large, permanent code comment) so the next person doesn't have to re-derive any of this, and left the actual mechanism exactly as-is: no `INSTALLABLE_FAMILIES` entry, no catalog change.** A follow-up with the full technical plan for whoever can safely provision test infrastructure is flagged separately.

10795	
10796	**What landed.** `scripts/import-thunderstore-catalog.ts` — the Thunderstore counterpart to
10797	`scripts/import-modrinth-catalog.ts`, same dry-run-by-default/`db-target-guard`/upsert-on-
10798	`@@unique([gameFamily, slug])`/idempotent shape. Pulls Thunderstore's real, open, unauthenticated v1
10799	catalogue API (`https://thunderstore.io/c/{community}/api/v1/package/` — one request per community
10800	returns its ENTIRE package list, no pagination, confirmed live) for four communities and writes real
10801	`GameMod` rows: **valheim** (gameFamily `valheim`, already had 21 hand-picked Phase 1 rows — this is a
10802	genuine bulk expansion onto them, not a from-scratch import), **sons-of-the-forest** (`sonsoftheforest`),
10803	**schedule-i** (`schedule1`), **sunkenland** (`sunkenland`) — all three family keys confirmed to already
10804	exist in `lib/games.ts`'s `GAME_FAMILIES` / `lib/game-control.ts`'s `GAME_CONTROL` before writing anything.
10805	
10806	**Quality gate (all documented in the script's own header, not repeated in full here).** Every
10807	community skips `is_deprecated` packages (real and large: 45.8% of valheim's raw 11,522) and
10808	`has_nsfw_content` packages, and skips anything tagged `Client-side` without also `Server-side` (this
10809	repo's own `GameMod.serverSide` doc comment: a client-only mod "cannot be installed on a server at all,
10810	and the catalogue should not offer it" — only valheim actually uses this tag pair in practice, removing
10811	1,204 client-only packages there). Valheim ALONE additionally requires the latest version's real
10812	download count `> 1,000` — its raw catalogue is 11,522 packages, so without a floor the "genuinely
10813	popular" signal would drown in near-zero-download noise; the other three communities are already small
10814	(81/523/45 raw) so no floor is applied there, matching "import what's there." Considered and rejected a
10815	Modrinth-style second disjoint pass on `rating_score` (Thunderstore's closest thing to Modrinth's
10816	"follows"): checked live how many packages a rating-based pass would catch that the downloads floor
10817	alone misses — zero, on this platform the two correlate too tightly for a second pass to add anything.
10818	
10819	**Legal / fetch-at-install-only (unchanged policy, re-verified this pass).** Thunderstore publishes no
10820	license field anywhere and has no Terms of Service at all — `license` is written `null` on every row
10821	(confirmed post-import: 0 of the resulting thunderstore rows carry a non-null license), never fabricated.
10822	Nothing was mirrored or rehosted: the script fetches only the catalogue JSON + hotlinks the real
10823	Thunderstore CDN icon URL; the actual mod file is still fetched at INSTALL TIME by
10824	`worker/game-mods.ts`'s existing `resolveUrl()`, unchanged.
10825	
10826	**Field semantics deliberately mirror `scripts/verify-gamemods.ts`'s existing `verifyThunderstore()`** —
10827	the periodic freshness pass that already runs against thunderstore rows and unconditionally overwrites
10828	`license`/`gameVersions`/`loaders`/`fileBytes`/`serverSide`/`galleryUrls` back to `null`/`[]` (its own
10829	endpoint doesn't expose richer versions of any of them). This import writes those same null/`[]` values
10830	up front, and defines `downloads`/`dependencyCount` the same way verify does (the LATEST version's own
10831	numbers, not a lifetime sum across version history) — so a value this script writes and a value the next
10832	verify run writes never disagree about what "downloads" means for the same package, and the catalogue's
10833	numbers don't flap on every cron cycle.
10834	
10835	**Slug strategy (why this isn't a plain slugify-and-go).** Real identity is Thunderstore's own
10836	`full_name` (`{owner}-{name}`, globally unique, stored as `sourceId` — the same value `resolveUrl()`
10837	already parses at install time). `slug` only needs to be unique per `gameFamily`, but Phase 1's 21

1	/**
2	 * Inject `-e TYPE=<VARIANT>` into a Minecraft OsTemplate's setupScript from
3	 * `Server.gameVariant` (the customer's checkout choice — vanilla/paper/purpur/
4	 * fabric/forge, see lib/game-config.ts's MINECRAFT.variants).
5	 *
6	 * Found live 2026-08-30: this substitution never existed anywhere in the
7	 * provisioning pipeline. The OsTemplate's setupScript is one static string
8	 * with no `TYPE` at all, so `gameVariant` was captured at checkout, stored on
9	 * `Server`, and then completely ignored — every Minecraft customer got plain
10	 * Vanilla regardless of what they picked (or paid for a plugin-support tier
11	 * and had their manually-installed plugins never load, since Vanilla has no
12	 * plugin API at all). Diagnosed via a real customer ticket: the fix here is
13	 * minecraft-specific by design (it's the only family with a real variant
14	 * concept today) — generalize via `schemaFor(family)` if another family gains
15	 * one, rather than hardcoding a second family name here.
16	 *
17	 * Explicit and idempotent: always injects a `TYPE`, even for "vanilla" —
18	 * removes any reliance on the image's own default ever staying Vanilla — and
19	 * is a no-op if the script already names an explicit `TYPE` (never override
20	 * something a future per-family script sets on purpose).
21	 *
22	 * Kept in its own side-effect-free module (rather than inline in
23	 * worker/index.ts) so it can be unit tested directly — importing
24	 * worker/index.ts runs its top-level `main()` job-polling loop.
25	 */
26	import { randomBytes } from "node:crypto";
27	import { schemaFor, minecraftImageForVersion } from "../lib/game-config";
28	import { isGameFamily, controlSpec, isSafeRemotePath } from "../lib/game-control";
29	import { dayzSteamCredentials } from "../lib/dayz-steam";
30	
31	function generatePassword(): string {
32	  // URL-safe, no ambiguous chars, 16 chars — same shape as worker/index.ts's
33	  // own generatePassword (kept as a small local copy rather than a shared
34	  // util, matching this codebase's existing convention — see also
35	  // worker/nxcloud.ts and lib/actions-company-mail.ts).
36	  return randomBytes(24).toString("base64url").replace(/[-_]/g, "x").slice(0, 16);
37	}
38	
39	export function applyGameVariant(setupScript: string, family: string | null, variant: string | null): string {
40	  if (family !== "minecraft") return setupScript;
41	  if (!variant) return setupScript;
42	  if (/-e\s+TYPE=/.test(setupScript)) return setupScript;
43	  const type = variant.toUpperCase();
44	  return setupScript.replace(/(docker run\s+(?:-d|--detach)\b)/, `$1 -e TYPE=${type}`);
45	}
46	
47	/**
48	 * Substitute the Minecraft image's Java-runtime tag to match the customer's
49	 * checkout-time VERSION choice.
50	 *
51	 * FOUND LIVE 2026-09-20: unlike every other customizable field, the
52	 * `itzg/minecraft-server` IMAGE TAG in `prisma/catalog.ts`'s setupScript is
53	 * not a `-e KEY=...` docker env var — it's the image reference itself — so
54	 * `applyGameConfigEnv` below (which only ever rewrites `-e KEY=` placeholders)
55	 * never touched it. Every Minecraft server was provisioned on the catalog's
56	 * static `:java21` regardless of the VERSION actually picked at checkout,
57	 * silently crash-looping any version needing a different Java (26.1+ needs
58	 * Java 25 — see lib/game-config.ts's MINECRAFT_JAVA_CUTOVERS for the real,
59	 * researched mapping and the live incident that found this).
60	 *
61	 * Deliberately minecraft-only and deliberately narrow: touches ONLY the
62	 * `itzg/minecraft-server(:tag)?` image reference, nothing else in the script.
63	 * Falls back to the schema's own VERSION default when the customer's
64	 * `gameConfig` doesn't carry one (an order that never touched the field) —
65	 * matching today's catalog default (1.21.1 -> java21) exactly, so a customer
66	 * who never touches VERSION sees no change in behavior.
67	 */
68	export function applyMinecraftJavaImage(
69	  setupScript: string,
70	  family: string | null,
71	  gameConfig: Record<string, unknown> | null | undefined
72	): string {
73	  if (family !== "minecraft") return setupScript;
74	  if (!/itzg\/minecraft-server(:[\w.-]+)?/.test(setupScript)) return setupScript;
75	  const version = gameConfig && gameConfig["VERSION"] != null ? String(gameConfig["VERSION"]) : "1.21.1";
76	  const image = minecraftImageForVersion(version);
77	  return setupScript.replace(/itzg\/minecraft-server(:[\w.-]+)?/, image);
78	}
79	
80	/**
81	 * The generalization this file's own docstring called for: substitute a
82	 * customer's checkout-time `Server.gameConfig` values into an OsTemplate's
83	 * setupScript, for whichever fields already appear in it as a docker
84	 * `-e KEY=...` env-var placeholder.
85	 *
86	 * Found live 2026-08-31 auditing DST (`dst` family): the whole per-family
87	 * customization schema in lib/game-config.ts (`ConfigField`, one per
88	 * `docker run -e KEY=...` in prisma/seed-wave4-games.ts and its Wave 1-3
89	 * predecessors) is captured at checkout into `Server.gameConfig`
90	 * (lib/game-order.ts) and shown in the post-deploy Settings tab, but — same
91	 * root cause as `applyGameVariant` above, just never generalized —
92	 * `provision()` in worker/index.ts never read it. Every family's setup
93	 * script always ran with its hardcoded static default (usually `''`),
94	 * regardless of what the customer entered at checkout. For most fields that
95	 * meant a cosmetically-wrong default (wrong MOTD, wrong hostname string);
96	 * for DST's `TOKEN` (an online DST cluster refuses to start with none — see
97	 * lib/game-config.ts's DST schema comment) it meant the container never
98	 * bound its port at all and PROVISION's own `checkGamePortOpen` health check
99	 * would time out and hard-fail the customer's paid order.
100	 *
101	 * Deliberately conservative: ONLY touches a key if the setupScript already
102	 * declares it as `-e KEY=...` — fields with no such placeholder (e.g. DST's
103	 * `PASSWORD`, which the yeetzone image never wired to an env var at all) are
104	 * left untouched rather than guessing a docker flag that isn't there.
105	 * Values are re-quoted as a single-quoted shell literal with proper `'`
106	 * escaping (`'\''`) so a customer-supplied string can never break out of the
107	 * quote and inject shell — the same safety property `validateConfig`'s own
108	 * control-character guard exists for, just extended to this second consumer
109	 * (a `docker run` command line) since the injection surface differs from a
110	 * line-oriented remote config file.
111	 */
112	/**
113	 * Substitute a freshly generated per-server secret into an OsTemplate's
114	 * setupScript, for a family whose image needs a real secret value that the
115	 * static catalog row can only ever leave blank — baking one directly into
116	 * the shared seed string (prisma/catalog.ts) would hand every future
117	 * customer the exact SAME value, since that row is one string shared by
118	 * every server of that family.
119	 *
120	 * Found live 2026-09-05 fixing a customer's "player list never loads"
121	 * ticket: the platform's own player-list/RCON feature (lib/game-control.ts)
122	 * requires Palworld's ADMIN_PASSWORD to be set (it doubles as the RCON auth
123	 * secret) and RCON's port published, but the catalog's setupScript set
124	 * neither — so no Palworld server, ever provisioned, could support the
125	 * player-list feature customers are paying for. RCON_ENABLED/RCON_PORT are
126	 * not secrets, so those went directly into prisma/catalog.ts's setupScript
127	 * string; only this one per-server value needs runtime substitution.
128	 *
129	 * Same conservative shape as applyGameConfigEnv: only touches a key that's
130	 * already present as `-e KEY=...` in the script, and the caller decides what
131	 * counts as a "secret" for a given family — this function has no per-family
132	 * knowledge of its own.
133	 */
134	export function applyGameControlSecrets(
135	  setupScript: string,
136	  secrets: Record<string, string>,
137	): string {
138	  let out = setupScript;
139	  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(secrets)) {
140	    const re = new RegExp(`-e\\s+${key}=(?:'[^']*'|"[^"]*"|\\S*)`);
141	    if (!re.test(out)) continue;
142	    const escaped = value.replace(/'/g, `'\\''`);
143	    out = out.replace(re, `-e ${key}='${escaped}'`);
144	  }
145	  return out;
146	}
147	
148	export function applyGameConfigEnv(
149	  setupScript: string,
150	  family: string | null,
151	  gameConfig: Record<string, unknown> | null | undefined,
152	): string {
153	  if (!family || !gameConfig) return setupScript;
154	  const schema = schemaFor(family);
155	  if (!schema) return setupScript;
156	  let out = setupScript;
157	  for (const field of schema.fields) {
158	    const raw = gameConfig[field.key];
159	    if (raw === undefined || raw === null) continue;
160	    // envKey lets a readable schema key (e.g. "world") differ from the
161	    // literal docker env var name the image expects (e.g. "WORLD_NAME") —
162	    // see ConfigField.envKey's doc comment in lib/game-config.ts.
163	    const envName = field.envKey ?? field.key;
164	    const re = new RegExp(`-e\\s+${envName}=(?:'[^']*'|"[^"]*"|\\S*)`);
165	    if (!re.test(out)) continue; // this field isn't docker-env-driven in this script — leave it alone
166	    const escaped = String(raw).replace(/'/g, `'\\''`);
167	    out = out.replace(re, `-e ${envName}='${escaped}'`);
168	  }
169	  return out;
170	}
171	
172	/**
173	 * If a GAME OsTemplate's setupScript installs the game via a detached
174	 * `docker run -d --name <container> ...` (true for every game image today —
175	 * see the OsTemplate rows for minecraft/terraria/ark/etc., all `docker run -d`),
176	 * rewrite the invocation to `docker create` and append a generated systemd unit
177	 * that starts/stops the container. Also caps the container's log driver
178	 * (`--log-opt max-size=10m --log-opt max-file=3`) — see the comment at the
179	 * `createCmd` line below for why.
180	 *
181	 * WHY THIS EXISTS: the whole game control panel — GAME_POWER start/stop/restart,
182	 * GAME_BACKUP, log tailing (lib/game-control.ts + worker/game-control.ts) —
183	 * resolves the running game exclusively via `systemctl cat <serviceHint>` /
184	 * `journalctl -u <unit>`. A bare `docker run -d` creates no systemd unit at all,
185	 * so every one of those lookups comes back empty and every control action fails
186	 * silently, on every game family, on every order. Found 2026-08-26 diagnosing a
187	 * customer's Terraria server (cmt9ss7ln000xhlrx0gch9fcx) that could never be
188	 * started/stopped from the dashboard even though PROVISION had completed
189	 * successfully — the container was in fact running, just entirely invisible to
190	 * systemd.
191	 *
192	 * The generated unit is named after the family's FIRST serviceHint, not the
193	 * docker container's own `--name` — the two don't always match (minecraft's
194	 * image runs as container "mc" but its control-spec hints are "minecraft" /
195	 * "minecraft-server") — so `systemctl cat <hint>` resolves regardless of what an
196	 * individual image's setup script happened to call its container.
197	 *
198	 * Intentionally conservative: any setupScript that doesn't match the exact
199	 * `docker run -d --name X ...` shape (or any non-game family, e.g. the
200	 * LAMP/WordPress/Caddy panel images that already install a real native systemd
201	 * service) is returned completely unchanged.
202	 *
203	 * Moved here from worker/index.ts 2026-09-24 (alongside `buildGameSetupScript`
204	 * below) so worker/game-control.ts — which worker/index.ts itself imports, so
205	 * it cannot import anything back from worker/index.ts without a circular
206	 * dependency — can also build a real reinstall script for the Danger Zone's
207	 * wipe/reinstall action. Purely a relocation: behavior is unchanged.
208	 */
209	export function wrapDockerGameService(setupScript: string, family: string | null): string {
210	  if (!isGameFamily(family)) return setupScript;
211	  const unitName = controlSpec(family)?.serviceHints[0];
212	  if (!unitName) return setupScript;
213	
214	  const re = /docker run\s+(?:-d|--detach)\b(.*?)\s+--name[= ]("?)([A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)\2(.*)$/.exec(setupScript.trim());
215	  if (!re) return setupScript;
216	  const [full, before, , containerName, after] = re;
217	  const matchIndex = setupScript.indexOf(full);
218	  if (matchIndex < 0) return setupScript;
219	
220	  // Strip docker's own restart policy — systemd now owns restart semantics for
221	  // this container, and leaving both in place makes the two supervisors fight
222	  // over a crash-looping process.
223	  const cleanedAfter = after.replace(/\s*--restart(?:=|\s+)\S+/, "");
224	  // Cap the container's json-file log driver. No game image's setupScript ever
225	  // set this, so a crash-looping container (systemd restarting it every 5s
226	  // forever — see RestartSec above) grows an unbounded log file. Root-caused
227	  // live 2026-09-17 on projectzomboid-kc0kcr: its docker json log alone had
228	  // grown to ~28 GB (on top of ~28.5 GB of rsyslog spamming its own
229	  // "no space left on device" write failures once the disk filled), filling
230	  // the 77 GB root disk to 100% and taking the game server down. This is the
231	  // single construction point every game family's `docker run` is rewritten
232	  // through, so applying the cap here covers all of them at once rather than
233	  // editing each family's setupScript individually. 10m x 3 files = a 30 MB
234	  // ceiling per container regardless of how long or how hard it crash-loops.
235	  const createCmd = `docker create --name ${containerName} --log-opt max-size=10m --log-opt max-file=3${before}${cleanedAfter}`
236	    .replace(/\s+/g, " ")
237	    .trim();
238	
239	  const prefix = setupScript.slice(0, matchIndex);
240	  const unit = [
241	    `cat > /etc/systemd/system/${unitName}.service <<'NXUNIT'`,
242	    "[Unit]",
243	    `Description=Nxeon game service (docker: ${containerName})`,
244	    "After=docker.service",
245	    "Requires=docker.service",
246	    "",
247	    "[Service]",
248	    `ExecStart=/usr/bin/docker start -a ${containerName}`,
249	    `ExecStop=/usr/bin/docker stop -t 30 ${containerName}`,
250	    "Restart=always",
251	    "RestartSec=5",
252	    "TimeoutStartSec=0",
253	    "",
254	    "[Install]",
255	    "WantedBy=multi-user.target",
256	    "NXUNIT",
257	    "systemctl daemon-reload",
258	    `systemctl enable --now ${unitName}`,
259	  ].join("\n");
260	
261	  return `${prefix}${createCmd}\n${unit}`;
262	}
263	
264	/**
265	 * Build the fully-substituted, systemd-wrapped game install script for a
266	 * server: variant → config values → Minecraft's java image tag → per-server
267	 * secrets → wrapped into a `docker create` + generated unit (see
268	 * `wrapDockerGameService`). Returns null for a non-game template (or one with
269	 * no setupScript at all).
270	 *
271	 * Extracted from `buildCloudInit` (2026-09-24) so `gameReinstall` (worker/
272	 * game-control.ts's GAME_REINSTALL handler) can regenerate the IDENTICAL
273	 * script an original PROVISION would have used — including reapplying
274	 * whatever gameVariant/gameConfig the customer has set SINCE the original
275	 * provision (a reinstall is exactly the moment a setting that silently never
276	 * applied gets a real chance to take effect), and minting BRAND NEW
277	 * per-server secrets for palworld/rust/cs2 on every call — the same
278	 * "reinstall rotates credentials, never keeps the old ones" rule
279	 * `reinstall()`'s own comment (worker/index.ts) applies to the VPS root
280	 * password.
281	 */
282	export function buildGameSetupScript(server: {
283	  osTemplate: { setupScript: string | null; family: string | null };
284	  gameVariant?: string | null;
285	  gameConfig?: unknown;
286	}): string | null {
287	  if (!server.osTemplate.setupScript) return null;
288	  const scriptWithVariant = applyGameVariant(server.osTemplate.setupScript, server.osTemplate.family, server.gameVariant ?? null);
289	  const scriptWithConfig = applyGameConfigEnv(
290	    scriptWithVariant,
291	    server.osTemplate.family,
292	    server.gameConfig as Record<string, unknown> | null,
293	  );
294	  const scriptWithJavaImage = applyMinecraftJavaImage(
295	    scriptWithConfig,
296	    server.osTemplate.family,
297	    server.gameConfig as Record<string, unknown> | null,
298	  );
299	  // dayz (Wave 11, 2026-09-24): shared Nxeon-owned Steam credential, not a
300	  // freshly-generated per-server secret — see lib/dayz-steam.ts. Unconfigured
301	  // resolves to an empty object, so applyGameControlSecrets' "only touches a
302	  // key already present" discipline leaves the setupScript's blank
303	  // placeholders exactly as seeded (honest SteamCMD anonymous-login failure
304	  // rather than silently proceeding). lib/game-order.ts also refuses new DayZ
305	  // orders while unconfigured, so this branch should never actually run
306	  // against an unconfigured account in production.
307	  const dayzCreds = dayzSteamCredentials();
308	  const dayzSecrets: Record<string, string> = dayzCreds ? { USERNAME: dayzCreds.username, PASSWRD: dayzCreds.password } : {};
309	  const scriptWithSecrets =
310	    server.osTemplate.family === "palworld"
311	      ? applyGameControlSecrets(scriptWithJavaImage, { ADMIN_PASSWORD: generatePassword() })
312	      : server.osTemplate.family === "rust"
313	        ? applyGameControlSecrets(scriptWithJavaImage, { RUST_RCON_PASSWORD: generatePassword() })
314	        : server.osTemplate.family === "cs2"
315	          ? applyGameControlSecrets(scriptWithJavaImage, { CS2_RCONPW: generatePassword() })
316	          : server.osTemplate.family === "armareforger"
317	            ? applyGameControlSecrets(scriptWithJavaImage, { ADMIN_PASSWORD: generatePassword() })
318	            : server.osTemplate.family === "dayz"
319	              ? applyGameControlSecrets(scriptWithJavaImage, dayzSecrets)
320	              : scriptWithJavaImage;
321	  return wrapDockerGameService(scriptWithSecrets, server.osTemplate.family);
322	}
323	
324	/**
325	 * Extract the docker `--name X` container name from a family's RAW (pre-wrap)
326	 * `docker run -d --name X ...` setupScript — the exact same regex
327	 * `wrapDockerGameService` above uses, exposed separately for
328	 * `gameReinstall` (worker/game-control.ts), which needs the real container
329	 * name to `docker rm -f` the old one before recreating it. Returns null if the
330	 * script doesn't match that shape (defensive; every current game setupScript
331	 * does).
332	 */
333	export function dockerContainerNameFrom(setupScript: string): string | null {
334	  const re = /docker run\s+(?:-d|--detach)\b.*?\s+--name[= ]("?)([A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)\1/.exec(setupScript.trim());
335	  return re ? re[2] : null;
336	}
337	
338	/**
339	 * Extract every `-v hostpath:containerpath` HOST-side path from a family's
340	 * RAW setupScript — sourced straight from the real `docker run -v ...` flags
341	 * (never guessed), so these are exactly the directories the game's own
342	 * container persists data to and the only ones a genuine "wipe" needs to
343	 * clear. Host paths never contain a colon in any current family's script, so
344	 * matching up to the first `:` reliably isolates the host side even when the
345	 * container side is itself quoted-with-spaces (The Isle's setupScript does
346	 * this: `-v /opt/theisle:"/home/steam/.../The Isle Dedicated Server"`).
347	 *
348	 * Safety-guarded, not just parsed: only returns paths that are both
349	 * `isSafeRemotePath` AND at least two segments under `/opt/` (every real game
350	 * mount observed in prisma/seed-wave*.ts is `/opt/<family>[/subdir]`) — this
351	 * is deliberately narrower than `isSafeRemotePath` alone so a malformed or
352	 * hand-edited OsTemplate row can never make a "wipe" target something as
353	 * broad as `/`, `/opt`, `/home`, or `/root`.
354	 */
355	export function dockerHostMountsFrom(setupScript: string): string[] {
356	  const out: string[] = [];
357	  const re = /-v\s+([^\s:]+):/g;
358	  let m: RegExpExecArray | null;

 * has no page-walking loop for the list step; the "pages" a normal importer
 * would burn through instead becomes one rate-limited detail call PER

 * SERVER-RELEVANCE FILTER: Vintage Story's ModDB publishes a real `side`
 * field per mod — "client" | "server" | "both" — set by the mod's own
 * author, not inferred. Checked the live distribution across all 8,684 mods:

There's substantial prior research to review now. I need to check the game-control library for service hints and containers across all families, then start planning the Phase 1 survey covering the remaining 39 families, starting with Palworld and its Linux mod support considerations.

For Palworld, I need to verify whether the thijsvanloef Docker image supports UE4SS mods on Linux since official Workshop support is Windows-only, and check whether Nexus mods can be manually installed.

For cs2, I'm checking whether joedwards32/cs2 supports Workshop map hosting via environment variables and how plugin frameworks like Metamod and CounterStrikeSharp integrate with the dedicated server mount.

I'm noting CS2 requires a hefty ~66GB download, making full verification expensive, so I may skip live testing for it. Then I'm moving to satisfactory, checking how wolveix/satisfactory-server handles dedicated server mods installed via ficsit-cli into the FactoryGame/Mods directory.

For satisfactory itself, mods appear to go manually into /config/gamefiles/FactoryGame/Mods with SML required, and ficsit.app exposes a real GraphQL API for mod versions and download links per target -- this looks like a solid candidate since the /opt/satisfactory:/config bind mount exists for SFTP placement. Then for sdtd, I'm checking that 7 Days to Die modlets go into serverfiles/Mods, which maps to the existing /opt/sdtd/serverfiles bind mount.

Since most 7DTD mods live on Nexus or community sites and Nexus gates direct downloads behind premium membership, I'm looking at whether vinanrra/7dtd-server has built-in mod installer flags instead, like toggles for Undead Legacy, Darkness Falls, or Ravenhearst as an alternative to scraping Nexus directly.

For V Rising, I'm checking whether trueosiris/vrising supports BepInEx under Wine so Thunderstore server mods can actually run, since that's the main mod distribution channel for that game.

Enshrouded seems to have no official or community server-side mod support worth documenting.

For Factorio, the factoriotools image has a real mechanism: mods placed in a bind-mounted directory plus an UPDATE_MODS_ON_START flag that reads mod-list.json and downloads from the mod portal using a username/token pair.

That said, downloading mods likely requires the factorio.com account to actually own the game, so I'll gate this honestly on customer-supplied credentials rather than pretending it's open access. Now moving on to gmod, which uses the ich777 steamcmd image.

For GMod, Workshop downloads on dedicated servers involve the `host_workshop_collection` launch parameter, and I need to check whether the `-authkey` Steam Web API key is still required or was deprecated around 2020. I also recall that dedicated servers can only pull in a single Workshop collection ID rather than a list of individual items.

There's another route worth considering: since GMod 13, servers can mount `.gma` files placed directly in the addons folder, so the ich777 image's steamcmd could download individual workshop items and copy the resulting .gma into garrysmod/addons rather than relying solely on the collection launch parameter.

Newer workshop items from steamcmd sometimes come as `_legacy.bin` files (LZMA-compressed) rather than plain `.gma`, which would need decompression before GMod could load them — something to verify. For Conan Exiles (item 9, melle2/conanexiles-ds), I'm now thinking through how its mod system reads workshop items into the ConanSandbox/Mods directory.

The Forest has no dedicated server modding support to speak of, so I'll mark that one as unsupported. Sons of the Forest is trickier though — RedLoader apparently does support dedicated servers, so I need to check whether the jammsen image accounts for that under Wine. Then moving on to Bedrock, which uses itzg's minecraft-bedrock-server image.

Bedrock's addon system is the mechanism, but the real problem is sourcing content — mcpedl has no API and CurseForge requires an API key, so I'd need to gate any integration on a CURSEFORGE_API_KEY being present, which I should check for in the .env. Finally, schedule1 isn't provisionable at all since there's no dedicated server binary, even though Thunderstore has plenty of mod listings for it.

Moving through the remaining games: dragonwilds has no dedicated-server mod support since it's early access; sunkenland has BepInEx mods on Thunderstore but I need to verify whether the melle2 server image actually supports BepInEx under Wine; abioticfactor relies on community UE4SS mods from Nexus with no official server-side support, so that's likely a no-go too. I'm now moving on to check corekeeper's server image and mod ecosystem.

For mod.io downloads, the files endpoint returns a binary_url that seems to work without heavy auth for public mods, though I should verify that. Moving to Icarus, I'm confirming it has no workshop or dedicated mod support, keeping it as none. For ARK: Survival Ascended, official mods come through CurseForge and the server needs a `-mods=` launch argument with mod IDs.

I should check whether there's a CurseForge key configured in .env before relying on that path. Moving to vintagestory: ich777's image looks like a strong candidate since the ModDB API exposes keyless download URLs for mainfile releases, with mods dropped into the Mods folder and requiring a restart. For necesse, mods come via Steam Workshop with andreasgl4ser's server image.

Necesse likely needs steamcmd to fetch the workshop jar and place it into the config mods folder, assuming the image bundles steamcmd for update purposes. Nightingale has no server-side mod support at all. content.content:
Unturned Linux Container with RocketMod 4 / RocketMod 5 / Vanilla support
# Unturned-Docker
This repository contains scripts for installing 64bit Unturned Linux with .NET 4.6.1 (optionally without docker).
It will auto-download the game on first start and download updates on each restart. It can detect crashes and auto restart in that case. Also it handles stdin/stdout correctly so you can have console input and output without the need for RCON.

# Getting Started
Images are hosted at `imperialplugins/unturned`. You can visit the [Docker Hub Repository](https://hub.docker.com/r/imperialplugins/unturned) for more information.

Example command to host a simple RocketMod 4 Unturned server:

`docker run -it -v <host_path>:/home/steam/Unturned -p 27015:27015 -p 27016:27016 -e SERVER_TYPE=rm4 --restart unless-stopped --name myserverinstance imperialplugins/unturned`

You can also append Unturned server args:
`docker run -it -v <host_path>:/home/steam/Unturned -p 27015:27015 -p 27016:27016 -e SERVER_TYPE=rm4 --restart unless-stopped --name myserverinstance imperialplugins/unturned -SkipAssets`

This will create a docker container that will listen on 27015 for Unturned and 27016 for Steam queries with RocketMod 4. 

You can also define STEAM_CMD_ARGS to run your own steamcmd commands on each restart:
`docker run -it -v <host_path>:/home/steam/Unturned -p 27015:27015 -p 27016:27016 -e STEAM_CMD_ARGS="+download_depot <somedepot>" -e SERVER_TYPE=rm4 --restart unless-stopped --name myserverinstance imperialplugins/unturned -SkipAssets`

## Server Type
The following are supported for the SERVER_TYPE environment variable:
* rm4 (installs RocketMod 4 module)
* rm5 (installs RocketMod 5 module)
* anything else or empty (does not install any modules)

## Building
To build, use `docker build . -t unturned`.

After building, you can start your server like the command in "Getting Started", but you will have to replace "imperialplugins/unturned" with just "unturned".

## Non-Docker Usage
First install required dependencies:
```sh
$ sudo apt-get install -y unzip tar curl coreutils lib32gcc1 libgdiplus
```

Set GAME_INSTALL_DIR, SERVER_NAME, GAME_ID (304930 for normal Unturned, 1110390 for dedicated Unturned), SERVER_TYPE environment variables:

```sh
$ export GAME_INSTALL_DIR=/path/to/Unturned
$ export SERVER_NAME=YOUR_SERVER_INSTANCE_NAME
$ export GAME_ID=1110390
$ export SERVER_TYPE=rm4
```

If you are not using the dedicated server app (1110390), you must also specify STEAM_USERNAME, STEAM_PASSWORD and STEAM_GUARD_TOKEN.
```sh
$ export STEAM_USERNAME=YourUsername
$ export STEAM_PASSWORD=YourPassword
$ export STEAM_GUARD_TOKEN=YourSteamGuardToken (if you have Steam Guard enabled)
```

You do not have to install steacmd, this script will do it for you. 

The script also supports $STEAM_CMD_ARGS which allows you to run your own steamcmd commands on each restart (e.g. `export STEAM_CMD_ARGS="+download_depot <somedepot>`)

Finally, run `init.sh` to install / update your server. It will automatically start the server afterwards:
```sh
$ ./init.sh 
```

You can also append Unturned server args like this:
```sh
$ ./init.sh -SkipAssets
```

content.content:
=== init.sh
#!/bin/bash

cd "$GAME_INSTALL_DIR" || exit

ulimit -n 2048

export TERM=xterm

if [ -d "./Unturned_Headless_Data" ]; then
    export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$LD_LIBRARY_PATH:`dirname $0`/Unturned_Headless_Data/Plugins/x86_64/
else
    export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$LD_LIBRARY_PATH:`dirname $0`/Unturned_Headless/Plugins/x86_64/
fi

if [ ! -d "$MODULES_DIR/Rocket.Unturned" ]; then
    if [ "$SERVER_TYPE" == "rm4" ]; then
      cp -rf "$GAME_INSTALL_DIR"/Extras/Rocket.Unturned/ "$GAME_INSTALL_DIR"/Modules/
    fi
fi

./Unturned_Headless.x86_64 -logfile 2>&1 -batchmode -nographics +secureserver/"$SERVER_NAME"=== Dockerfile
FROM ubuntu:bionic

LABEL maintainer="Enes Sadık Özbek <es.ozbek.me>"

ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND noninteractive
ENV GAME_INSTALL_DIR /home/steam/Unturned
ENV GAME_ID 1110390
ENV SERVER_NAME server
ENV STEAM_USERNAME anonymous
ENV STEAMCMD_DIR /home/steam/steamcmd

EXPOSE 27015
EXPOSE 27016

VOLUME ["$GAME_INSTALL_DIR"]

# Install required packages
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y unzip tar curl coreutils lib32gcc1 libgdiplus && \
    apt-get clean -y && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* /tmp/* /var/tmp/*

# Add Steam user
RUN adduser \
	--home /home/steam \
	--disabled-password \
	--shell /bin/bash \
	--gecos "user for running steam" \
	--quiet \
	steam

USER steam
WORKDIR $STEAMCMD_DIR

RUN mkdir -p $GAME_INSTALL_DIR

# Install Unturned
RUN curl -s https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/client/installer/steamcmd_linux.tar.gz | tar -vxz && \
    bash ./steamcmd.sh +force_install_dir $GAME_INSTALL_DIR +login $STEAM_USERNAME $STEAM_PASSWORD $STEAM_GUARD_TOKEN $STEAM_CMD_ARGS +@sSteamCmdForcePlatformBitness 64 +app_update $GAME_ID +quit && \
    mkdir -p /home/steam/.steam/sdk64/ && \
    cp -f linux64/steamclient.so /home/steam/.steam/sdk64/steamclient.so

WORKDIR $STEAMCMD_DIR

COPY init.sh .

ENTRYPOINT ["./init.sh"]

# Mods on Dedicated Server

The dedicated server does **not** require actual mod files to be copied. According to the documentation:

"Dedicated server does not require any additional DLC or mod data. Everything needed is handled via server_packages.sii and server_packages.dat files."

Additionally, the page states that "server_packages.sii and server_packages.dat must be generated manually via calling the `export_server_packages` command while normal game is running. Generated configuration will mirror your game configuration."

In summary, you only need to export the configuration files from a client—not the mod files themselves.

Since the prod worker processes jobs serially, a game server provision could block the queue for up to 45 minutes during install, which would delay real customer jobs like power, backups, or mod installs — a real production concern worth checking further to confirm whether the provision call actually blocks synchronously inside runJob.

A better approach: instead of running full test provisions through the worker queue, I could order a plain VPS (quick, no game-install wait) on node-5, then SSH in and run the same setupScript manually out-of-band. That keeps the worker queue free of long-running test jobs while still validating the exact same install script.

I'm also considering whether I could test multiple game families on a single VPS sequentially, since running them simultaneously risks port conflicts (e.g. kf2 and unturned both using 27015).

Ultimately I think a plain VPS order running the exact same provisioning script (docker create plus systemd unit) counts as a genuine real-world test, even if the orchestration differs slightly from cloud-init — the mod code path only cares about the running container, mounts, and systemd unit, so I'll note that distinction honestly in the report.

I should pick a VPS plan with enough headroom, something like 8GB RAM / 80GB disk to comfortably cover KF2 and similar titles, sizing up for heavier games like Conan if needed. Provisioning goes through the platform's serialized queue too, so my job would still wait behind the current terraria job, but going through the platform rather than hitting Proxmox directly is safer since it handles VMID allocation, IPAM, and port forwarding correctly.

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

  ## 1. NECESSE
  **docker run:** `andreasgl4ser/necesse-server:latest`, `-v /opt/necesse:/home/necesse/.config/Necesse`
  
  **1. Image source (VERIFIED):** GitHub `andreas-glaser/necesse-docker-server` (both `master` and `main` branches, identical content, read directly). Files read: `Dockerfile`, `entrypoint.sh`.
  - Game/server binary installs to `/app` (SteamCMD `force_install_dir /app/`, appid **1169370** = dedicated-server app, anonymous login).
  - The game's actual data/config dir is `/home/necesse/.config/Necesse` (Dockerfile: `VOLUME ["/home/necesse/.config/Necesse"]`) — this **is** the host-reachable path: `/opt/necesse`.
  - `/app` (where Server.jar and entrypoint.sh live) is **NOT** bind-mounted in the production `docker run` — only the config/data volume is.
  
  **2. Image-level mod support (VERIFIED — NONE):** Read the full `entrypoint.sh`. Its `launch_server()` builds the java command line strictly from ~20 named env vars (`WORLD_NAME`, `SERVER_PORT`, `DATA_DIR`, `LOGS_DIR`, etc. — quoted in full below). There is **no** `MODS=`, `MOD_DIR=`, `WORKSHOP_IDS=`, or generic passthrough-args env var anywhere in the script or Dockerfile `ENV` block.
  
  **3. Game-level mod mechanism (VERIFIED, official wiki https://necessewiki.com/Modding, fetched and quoted directly):**
  > "For dedicated servers to have mods, they must find and download the mod jar file... put it inside a mods folder... Windows dedicated Server over steamcmd: ... edit the server start parameters ... `-jar Server.jar -nogui -datadir .\data -mod .\mods` ... copy your .jar mod files ... into the mods folder. The server will recognize on startup the mods in the folder and loads them."
  - Mechanism: **launch-argument-driven local folder**, `-mod <path>`. No native auto-download-from-Workshop launch arg exists — confirmed against the official `-help` output (community-sourced via Steam discussions) which lists `-help,-nogui,-settings,-world,-port,-slots,-owner,-motd,-logging,-zipsaves,-language,-ip,-localdir` and nothing mod-related.
  - Client-side workshop-subscribed mods land at `~/.config/Necesse/mods` (same wiki), but that's the **client**, not this dedicated-server image.
  
  **4. Mod source (VERIFIED via live Steam Web API test):** Steam Workshop, appid **1169040** (client app — confirmed: `GetPublishedFileDetails` on a real mod id `3445509102` returned `creator_app_id/consumer_app_id: 1169040`). Tested `ISteamRemoteStorage/GetPublishedFileDetails/v1/` (no key needed) — result: `file_url` is **empty**, `hcontent_file` is set (non-zero) → the file is stored as Steam depot/UGC content, **not** directly HTTP-downloadable. Programmatic download without credentials we lack is **not possible** via the Web API; would require `steamcmd +login anonymous +workshop_download_item 1169040 <id>`. Whether Necesse's Steamworks settings have "anonymous game servers can download workshop items" enabled is **UNKNOWN** — I found no confirming or denying community report for this specific appid, and could not test steamcmd here (no install allowed on this host).
  
  **5. Ships steamcmd? VERIFIED — yes,** baked into the image at build time at `/steamapps/steamcmd.sh` (Dockerfile: `mkdir -p /steamapps && curl ... steamcmd_linux.tar.gz | tar zxvf - -C /steamapps`; entrypoint references `${STEAMCMD_DIR}/steamcmd.sh` where `STEAMCMD_DIR=/steamapps`). Persisted in the image layer (not the bind mount).

  - Place downloaded `.jar` mod files at host `/opt/necesse/mods/` (a new subfolder under the already-mounted config dir).
  - The stock entrypoint has no way to add `-mod /home/necesse/.config/Necesse/mods` to the java command via env vars, so this requires either (a) `docker exec necesse sed -i` to insert the flag into `/app/entrypoint.sh` inside the running container, then `docker restart` (not recreate — a restart reuses the same writable layer so the patched script persists), or (b) recreate the container with `--entrypoint` overridden to a one-line wrapper that execs java directly with `-mod` added. Both are one-time, non-declarative workarounds — this is not a supported image feature.
  - No confirmed boot-log line for "mod loaded" was found in any source (UNKNOWN) — would need to observe a live boot.
  
  **7. Example mods (real, confirmed via Steam Web API):** `3534267732` (RPG Mod v0.7 — requires deps, skip for smoke test), `3618901624` ("Necesse base"), `3416719851` ("MODS NECESSE"). Best simple pick found: `3445509102` ("Race Mod (ALPHA)", 672KB, but author calls it abandoned — pick a smaller/simpler item if possible; I did not have time to vet every candidate for zero-dependency).
  
  **8. Verdict:** **GATED** (real mechanism = download-and-place, but blocked on: (a) entrypoint has no `-mod` passthrough — needs an image/entrypoint patch, not just an env change; (b) UNKNOWN whether anonymous steamcmd workshop download works for appid 1169040 — if not, Nxeon has no owning Steam account for Necesse either). Confidence: **medium** (mechanism itself is well-documented; the blocking factors are concrete but the anonymous-download question is untested).
  
  ================================================================
  ## 2. STATIONEERS
  **docker run:** `didstopia/stationeers-server:latest`, `-v /opt/stationeers:/steamcmd/stationeers`
  
  **1. Image source (VERIFIED):** GitHub `Didstopia/stationeers-server`. Files read: `Dockerfile`, `start_stationeers.sh`, `install.txt`, `README.md`.
  - Base image `didstopia/base:nodejs-22-steamcmd-ubuntu-24.04`. `install.txt`: `force_install_dir /steamcmd/stationeers`, `login anonymous`, `app_update 600760 validate` (600760 = dedicated-server appid, distinct from client 544550).

  **2. Image-level mod support (VERIFIED — none documented):** README lists only `STATIONEERS_SERVER_STARTUP_ARGUMENTS`, `_SERVER_NAME`, `_WORLD_NAME`, `_SERVER_SAVE_INTERVAL`, `_GAME_PORT`, `_QUERY_PORT`, `_SERVER_PASSWORD`. No mod/workshop env var. **However**, `STATIONEERS_SERVER_STARTUP_ARGUMENTS` (default `"-autostart -nographics -batchmode"`) is a **free-form string appended to the launch command** (confirmed in `start_stationeers.sh`: `STATIONEERS_STARTUP_COMMAND=$(echo "$STATIONEERS_SERVER_STARTUP_ARGUMENTS" | tr -s " ")`, then more flags appended) — so this env var IS a usable passthrough if the game has a real mod-related launch flag (see below, inconclusive).
  
  **3. Game-level mod mechanism (COMMUNITY-EVIDENCE, multiple independent hosting-provider sources + a live Steam discussion thread, consistent with each other):**
  - Mods are configured via a `ModConfig.xml` (schema confirmed via citadelservers.com KB, quoted exactly):
  ```xml
  <ModConfig ...>
  <Mods><unsignedLong>1</unsignedLong><unsignedLong>1001</unsignedLong></Mods>
  <DisabledMods></DisabledMods>
  <LocalMods><LocalMod><folder>3570726509</folder><modID>1001</modID></LocalMod></LocalMods>
  </ModConfig>
  ```
    (`1` = built-in core mod always present; each additional mod gets a sequential internal id in `<Mods>`, mapped in `<LocalMods>` to a `<folder>` — the folder is literally named with the Steam Workshop id.)

  - The dedicated server does **not** appear to auto-download from Steam Workshop itself — mods must be manually placed (download-and-place), matching the "Dedicated servers ... requires additional manual configuration — direct file access and editing" language from multiple host KBs (xgamingserver.com, gamehostbros.com).
  
  **4. Mod source (VERIFIED via live Steam Web API):** Steam Workshop, appid **544550** (client — confirmed: 3 real mods tested, all `consumer_app_id: 544550`, `file_url` empty in all cases → same UGC-depot situation as Necesse, needs `steamcmd workshop_download_item 544550 <id>`). Whether anonymous steamcmd download works for 544550 is **UNKNOWN** — no confirming evidence found either way.
  
  **5. Ships steamcmd? VERIFIED — yes, but ephemeral.** `start_stationeers.sh` re-downloads steamcmd fresh on **every container start**: `curl -s http://media.steampowered.com/installer/steamcmd_linux.tar.gz | tar -v -C /steamcmd -zx`, landing at `/steamcmd/steamcmd.sh`. It's not baked into the image, but it IS present in every running container (outside the `/steamcmd/stationeers` bind-mounted subfolder, so it doesn't persist to host, but is always freshly available via `docker exec`).
  
  **6. Concrete recipe:** Download mod content (steamcmd, gated as above) → extract into `/opt/stationeers/rocketstation_DedicatedServer_Data/StreamingAssets/Data/mods/<WorkshopID>/` → write/edit a `ModConfig.xml` at the game's root config location referencing that folder+sequential id → `docker restart` (a restart should suffice since it's just game data/config, not an entrypoint change). No confirmed boot-log line found (UNKNOWN).
  
  **7. Example mods (real, confirmed via Steam Web API):** `3534704980` ("Suit Control 1.0", 244KB, IC-Code tag, no listed dependency — good smoke-test candidate), `3589116234` ("Motorbikes", 1.86MB, adds craftable vehicle, no BepInEx mentioned). Avoid `3571616762` — its description explicitly requires BepInEx/StationeersLaunchPad (a plugin framework), not dependency-free.
  
  **8. Verdict:** **GATED** (download-and-place mechanism is real and consistent across independent sources, but blocked on: UNKNOWN anonymous-steamcmd-download status for appid 544550, same as Necesse). For mod.io-based games, Mordhau needs Mods set in Game.ini plus a ServerModAuthToken, but this requires an actual mod.io OAuth token rather than just an API key, so it's gated on obtaining that.

Actually, mod.io API keys can still fetch public mod file binary_urls without OAuth, so Mordhau could work by having the worker resolve and download the .pak directly into the CustomPaks folder — no token needed for that path. The catch is this only works for server-side-only utility mods; content mods like maps or skins still require clients to auto-download via the server's Mods= list, which does need the OAuth token.

Sandstorm remains gated due to email-code login, seccomp restrictions, and a missing volume. For ARK: Survival Ascended, mods are set through a MODS env var using CurseForge project IDs, letting the server self-download — but without a CurseForge API key I'd need to scrape public pages for a small curated seed of project IDs, and the server itself is a heavy ~12GB+ download needing a beefier RAM plan, making verification costly despite the simple mechanism.

Sorting priorities into tiers: Tier 1 for building and live-verifying includes vintagestory, barotrauma, necesse, gmod, kf2, and corekeeper. Tier 2 covers conan, stationeers, eco, arkasa, armareforger, sdtd, and satisfactory — build now, verify if time allows. Tier 3 holds the gated or deferred ones: factorio, mordhau, sandstorm, spaceengineers, dayz, cs2, cs16, bedrock, icarus, abioticfactor, the BepInEx trio, and palworld. That's a lot to juggle, so I need to stay pragmatic about what actually gets built.

I'm second-guessing KF2's disk footprint since the dedicated server install might run closer to 16GB against a 20GB budget, which feels risky, so I'll hold off deciding on it. My plan is to implement vintagestory first and verify it live, then queue up barotrauma and necesse test server provisioning in parallel since they're quick, followed by implementing both using a generic steamcmd-in-container helper, then move on to provisioning gmod and corekeeper given their modest disk requirements.

content.thinking:
Vintage Story support is now fully verified with version-matched installs, dependency auto-resolution, incompatible version refusal, and removal. Now I'm designing a generic steamcmd-in-container helper for other Workshop-based games that need item downloads placed into their mod folders, which will run steamcmd inside the game's container with an anonymous login and a temporary install directory.

I'm weighing two approaches: reusing the existing pattern where L4D2/PZ call steamcmd already present on the container's PATH, versus spinning up a throwaway `cm2network/steamcmd` container on the VM independent of any game image. The throwaway container is more uniform across families and avoids depending on each image's steamcmd path or user permissions, though it costs an extra ~170MB image pull on first use -- I'm leaning toward the throwaway approach for consistency and to keep Valve's tool running on the customer's own VM as intended.

Now I'm checking whether using each game image's built-in steamcmd binary instead would avoid the extra pull, since several images (Barotrauma, Necesse, GMod, Conan, Stationeers) each ship their own steamcmd at different paths.

Actually, maybe I should just use each game container's own steamcmd via docker exec, downloading into a bind-mounted path so the host can access results directly, which avoids needing extra images. For Barotrauma specifically I'd run the workshop download command targeting a path inside the mount, but I need to check whether the container's default exec user has permission to write there since the image may run as root or drop to a steam user.

Root should work fine even if steamcmd complains a bit. Now let me check the actual running status of the Barotrauma and Necesse servers to see where things stand.

FROM ich777/debian-baseimage
LABEL org.opencontainers.image.authors="admin@minenet.at"
LABEL org.opencontainers.image.source="https://github.com/ich777/docker-steamcmd-server"
RUN apt-get update && \
	apt-get -y install --no-install-recommends lib32gcc-s1 lib32stdc++6 && \
	rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
ENV DATA_DIR="/serverdata"
ENV STEAMCMD_DIR="${DATA_DIR}/steamcmd"
ENV SERVER_DIR="${DATA_DIR}/serverfiles"
ENV GAME_ID="template"
ENV GAME_NAME="template"
ENV GAME_PARAMS="template"
ENV GAME_PORT=27015
ENV VALIDATE=""
ENV UMASK=000
ENV UID=99

#!/bin/bash
source "${SCRIPTSDIR}/helper-functions.sh"

MODIO_CORE_KEEPER_ENDPOINT="${MODIO_API_URL}/games/@corekeeper/mods"

download_and_install_mod() {
  if [ -z "${MODIO_API_KEY}" ]; then
    LogError "MODIO_API_KEY is required for downloading mods"
    exit 1
  fi

  local mod_string_id="$1"
  local version="$2"

  # The mod.io API needs the mod string id to be prefixed with @
  local modio_mod_endpoint="${MODIO_CORE_KEEPER_ENDPOINT}/@${mod_string_id}"
  local download_url
  local actual_version

  local mod_info
  mod_info=$(curl -s "${modio_mod_endpoint}?api_key=${MODIO_API_KEY}")

  if [ -z "$mod_info" ]; then
    LogError "Failed to get mod info for mod ${mod_string_id}"
    exit 1
  fi

  local mod_name
  mod_name=$(echo "$mod_info" | jq -r ".name")

  if [ -n "$version" ]; then
    # Get all files for the mod
    local mod_files
    mod_files=$(curl -s "${modio_mod_endpoint}/files?api_key=${MODIO_API_KEY}")

    if [ -z "$mod_files" ]; then
      LogError "Failed to get mod files for ${mod_name} (${mod_string_id})"
      exit 1
    fi

    # Find the specified version
    download_url=$(echo "$mod_files" | jq -r ".data[] | select(.version == \"${version}\") | .download.binary_url")
    if [ -z "$download_url" ] || [ "$download_url" = "null" ]; then
      LogError "Version ${version} not found for mod ${mod_name} (${mod_string_id})"
      exit 1
    fi
    actual_version="$version"
  else
    # Use latest version
    download_url=$(echo "$mod_info" | jq -r ".modfile.download.binary_url")
    actual_version=$(echo "$mod_info" | jq -r ".modfile.version")
  fi

  if [ -z "$download_url" ] || [ "$download_url" = "null" ]; then
    LogError "Failed to get download URL for mod ${mod_name} (${mod_string_id})"
    exit 1
  fi

  # Create temp directory for download
  local temp_dir
  temp_dir=$(mktemp -d)
  local temp_mod_download="${temp_dir}/${mod_string_id}.zip"

  local mod_dir="${MODSDIR}/${mod_string_id}"

  # Download and extract mod
  if curl -s -L "${download_url}?api_key=${MODIO_API_KEY}" -o "${temp_mod_download}"; then
    # Create mod directory and extract
    mkdir -p "${mod_dir}"
    unzip -q "${temp_mod_download}" -d "${mod_dir}"
    LogInfo "Installed ${mod_name} (${mod_string_id}) ${actual_version}"
  else
    LogError "Failed to install ${mod_name} (${mod_string_id}) ${actual_version}"
    exit 1
  fi

  # Cleanup
  rm -rf "${temp_dir}"
}

install_mods() {
  # Split the comma-separated list of mods
  IFS=',' read -ra mod_list <<< "$MODS"

  for mod_spec in "${mod_list[@]}"; do
    # Trim whitespace
    mod_spec=$(echo "$mod_spec" | tr -d '[:space:]')
    [ -z "$mod_spec" ] && continue

    local mod_string_id
    local version
    # Split into id and version
    if [[ "$mod_spec" =~ ":" ]]; then
      mod_string_id="${mod_spec%%:*}" # Everything before the colon
      version="${mod_spec#*:}" # Everything after the colon
    else
      mod_string_id="$mod_spec"
      version=""
    fi

    download_and_install_mod "$mod_string_id" "$version"
  done
}

manage_mods() {
  # We always clear the mods directory so the installed mods reflect exactly what was specified by the user
  rm -rf "${MODSDIR}"
  mkdir -p "${MODSDIR}"

  if [[ "${MODS_ENABLED,,}" != "true" ]]; then
    LogInfo "MODS_ENABLED is not true, skipping mod installation"
    return 0
  fi

  if [ -z "${MODS}" ]; then
    LogWarn "MODS_ENABLED is true but there are no mods specified"
    return 0
  fi

  LogInfo "Installing mods..."
  install_mods
}

content.thinking:
I'm trying to pin down where Conan Exiles stores its modlist.txt and userdir paths, and recalling whether the dedicated server supports a ServerModList or -ModList flag for specifying mods at launch.

Actually, a bigger concern surfaces: the current Steam release is the UE5 "Conan Exiles Enhanced," and the prod setupScript doesn't set the required GAME_UE5=true flag the image README says is now mandatory — meaning ConanSandboxServer.exe may no longer even start in prod. I'm weighing whether to flag this as a broken-server risk rather than verify it live, since the download path itself (anonymous 440900) is confirmed working.

I'll leave Conan documented as an unverified follow-up rather than wiring it live. Turning to the remaining buildable set — gmod and necesse are queued for verification, kf2 is built but hard to verify given disk constraints, stationeers needs live exploration, and armareforger looks promising since its mod mechanism (MODS_JSON_B64 self-download from Bohemia Workshop) is verified in source; I'm now considering whether the Reforger workshop site exposes a Next.js data API I could scrape to seed a real mod catalog, though live provisioning to confirm it would carry a moderate disk cost.

For arkasa, the self-download mechanism relies on CurseForge IDs, but CurseForge is Cloudflare-blocked and its API needs a key — I could still build the mechanism and seed a small curated set from scraped pages, though full ASA verification would be too resource-heavy to run live, so I'd build without live-verifying.

Looking at the rest of the games: sdtd needs a mod URL mechanism seeded from DonovanMods with a heavy 15GB download, satisfactory uses the ficsit API with medium-heavy resource needs, sunkenland and sotf both run BepInEx through Wine with existing Thunderstore rows making them medium-difficulty builds, and vrising currently has no rows so it would need a fresh Thunderstore import.

Given queue-blocking concerns and limited time, I'll prioritize gmod and necesse for live testing, add armareforger with both build and live verification, treat sunkenland as a stretch goal, and leave kf2 built but not live-verified — documenting everything else for later. Each provision test does block real customer jobs in the queue, but Reforger installs in about 5 minutes and Sunkenland's Wine setup takes 5-10 minutes, so the impact should be manageable while I look into Reforger's workshop data access.

content.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -e

# Check if .X1-lock file exists and remove. Otherwise Xvfb cannot start.
[ -f /tmp/.X1-lock ] && rm -f /tmp/.X1-lock

_terminate() {
  echo "Caught TERM signal!"
  echo "Stopping Sunkenland"
  wineserver -k -w
  /etc/init.d/xvfb stop
}

trap _terminate HUP INT QUIT TERM

if [ -z "${GAME_WORLD_GUID}" ]; then
  echo "Please set environment variable 'GAME_WORLD_GUID', game cannot start otherwise."
  exit 1
fi

if [ -z "${GAME_REGION}" ]; then
  GAME_REGION=eu
fi

if [[ ${GAME_MAX_PLAYER} =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
  MAX_PLAYER_PARAM=" -maxPlayerCapacity ${GAME_MAX_PLAYER}"
fi

if [ "${GAME_SESSION_INVISIBLE}" = true ]; then
  SESSION_INVISIBLE=" -makeSessionInvisible true"
fi

if [ "$GAME_UPDATE" = true ] || [ -z "$(ls -A /sunkenland/game)" ]; then
  if [ -n "${GAME_BETA_VERSION}" ]; then
    BETA_VERSION=" -beta ${GAME_BETA_VERSION}"
    echo "Updating to beta version ${GAME_BETA_VERSION}"
  fi
  echo "Start game update..."
  steamcmd +force_install_dir /${USER_NAME}/game +@sSteamCmdForcePlatformType windows +login anonymous +app_update \
           "${APP_ID}" ${BETA_VERSION} validate +quit
  echo "Game update done"
fi

/etc/init.d/xvfb start
wine /${USER_NAME}/game/Sunkenland-DedicatedServer.exe -nographics -batchmode -worldGuid ${GAME_WORLD_GUID}${MAX_PLAYER_PARAM}${SESSION_INVISIBLE} -password "${GAME_PASSWORD}" -region "${GAME_REGION}" &

wait
FROM melle2/wine-steamcmd-ubuntu:24.04-3

ENV USER_NAME=sunkenland \
    APP_ID=2667530
ENV WORLD_FOLDER="/${USER_NAME}/.wine/drive_c/users/${USER_NAME}/AppData/LocalLow/Vector3 Studio/Sunkenland/"

ARG USER_ID=7000
ARG GROUP_ID=7000


RUN groupadd -g ${USER_ID} ${USER_NAME} && useradd -d /${USER_NAME} -u ${USER_ID} -g ${GROUP_ID} -m ${USER_NAME} && \
    mkdir ${USER_NAME}/.steam/ ${USER_NAME}/game && chown ${USER_ID}:${GROUP_ID} ${USER_NAME}/.steam ${USER_NAME}/game

ADD startSunkenland.sh /${USER_NAME}
RUN chmod 744 /${USER_NAME}/startSunkenland.sh && chown ${USER_ID}:${GROUP_ID} /${USER_NAME}/startSunkenland.sh

USER ${USER_NAME}
WORKDIR /${USER_NAME}
ENV WINEDEBUG=fixme-all,err+all
ENV XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="/tmp/runtime-sunnkenland"

RUN mkdir -p ${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR} && chmod 700 ${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR} && chown ${USER_ID}:${GROUP_ID} ${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR} && \
    wine wineboot -i && wineserver -w && \
    wine reg delete "HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\winebth" /f && wineserver -k && \
    mkdir -p "${WORLD_FOLDER}" && ln -s "/${USER_NAME}/Worlds" "${WORLD_FOLDER}"

ENTRYPOINT ["./startSunkenland.sh"]

EXPOSE 27015
