content.thinking:
I need to make sure the temporary verification files under scripts/ don't get committed. While that runs, I'll start drafting the documentation, beginning with the Phase 1 survey table covering all 39 non-wired families plus the 12 already-wired ones and terraria.

For the already-wired dozen — minecraft, rust, valheim (download-and-place), ark, unturned (with its path bug now fixed), dst, squad, soulmask, projectzomboid, tf2, l4d2, empyrion — those are settled, and terraria stays out of scope since it's being handled in parallel.

Going through the 39 candidates: Palworld's workshop support is Windows-only with no real mod plumbing on Linux, and the unofficial UE4SS port relies on third-party native code, so it needs owner sign-off and stays unwired. CS2 does have a real workshop path through environment variables plus a Metamod/CSS plugin flow, but since the install size makes it currently unsellable against typical plan sizes, there's no server to verify against, so I'm deferring it as a follow-up. Satisfactory has a genuine new modding source via ficsit.app with SML as a dependency, so I'm wiring it up and noting verification is still pending.

7 Days to Die has native mod URL support built into the image, but without a curated catalog and given DLL mods require EAC disabled, it needs more groundwork before wiring. V Rising's BepInEx path through Thunderstore looks workable under Wine but hasn't been live-tested and requires DLL override configuration the image doesn't currently support. Enshrouded is gated behind Nexus API keys for its content despite having a community loader. Factorio is fully gated since the Mod Portal requires an authenticated token that returned a 403 in testing, though the catalog itself has thousands of entries ready once an account exists — I'm noting the token should be resolved at the worker level so it never touches the VM. GMod, on the other hand, has a clean real path through anonymous steamcmd workshop downloads, so I'm wiring it with verification still pending.

Moving on, Conan Exiles has a real anonymous-download path but I'm flagging that the production setup script is missing a flag the image README now says is mandatory, meaning the game might not even boot currently. The Forest has no viable server-side mod support at all — only a Windows GUI tool. Sons of the Forest has a plausible BepInEx IL2CPP route under Wine but needs classification work to separate actual mods from manager tools in its catalog. Bedrock supports native behavior packs but lacks any real bulk content source since the community sites don't offer APIs. Schedule1 isn't relevant since it has no dedicated server. Dragonwilds has real pak-based mod support but its content is locked behind Nexus/CurseForge keys. Sunkenland looks similarly BepInEx-based with a small Thunderstore catalog that also needs filtering out mod manager entries.

Abiotic Factor has some GitHub-based UE4SS mods but no real catalog since mod.io hasn't actually launched support despite announcements. Core Keeper is tricky — the image wipes its mod folder on every boot and re-pulls via its own mod.io key, which would expose Nxeon's credentials to every customer as root, so this needs an ownership decision before wiring anything. Icarus has workable pak-based mods from GitHub but no catalog and strict client-matching requirements. ARK: Survival Ascended can self-download CurseForge mods by project ID without needing a key for installation, but building an actual catalog requires a CurseForge API key, which is blocked by their Cloudflare protection — so the install mechanism could technically work even though the catalog side remains ungated.

Vintage Story is fully wired and verified through ModDB. Necesse uses anonymous steamcmd inside the container to pull jars into the mods directory — wired but pending confirmation of the default mods path. Nightingale has no loader by design.

Space Engineers should theoretically work through Sandbox config mod items letting the dedicated server self-download from Steam Workshop, but I haven't live-tested it and a sample workshop item returned File Not Found under anonymous steamcmd, so downloading under Wine is unverified. Killing Floor 2 has a legitimate env-var mechanism for subscribing to workshop items that the server then self-downloads, but it's not live-verified and the depot size alone (~20 GiB) exceeds the entry-tier 20GB disk plan, which is its own sizing problem worth flagging. Barotrauma's mod mechanism via LocalMods and config_player.xml looks real too, though the anonymous workshop download path still needs verification.

Now the dedicated server itself is failing anonymous install with a "Missing configuration" error, meaning Barotrauma can't even be provisioned right now — that's a hard blocker, not wired. Sandstorm is gated because mod.io self-download needs a server-owned account with email-code login plus a seccomp profile and volume, none of which exist in the production docker setup. Mordhau's real path needs a mod.io OAuth token that's currently unavailable, so it's gated, and the server-side CustomPaks route is unverified. The Isle is essentially dead for modding since Workshop was dissolved and pak mods now scatter through Discord, while UE4SS requires Windows/Wine on what's a native Linux image. Stationeers has a community-tier mods folder mechanism that's verified for anonymous download but untested live. Eco looks solid — mod.io game id 6 lets you download and place signed binaries into the Mods folder.

Empyrion is already wired. The Plutonium and IW5 variants don't apply since there's no OsTemplate or GamePlan in production for them. Arma Reforger has a real path through a base64-encoded MODS_JSON env var that lets the server self-download from Bohemia's Reforger Workshop — this needs a new source and importer, and it's wired pending verification. CS16 has AMXX baked into the image with straightforward plugin placement, but the catalog is mostly engine replacements rather than plugins, and GitHub's API rate limit got exhausted during research. ETS2/ATS need no mod files at all since mods come through server_packages exported from a client per SCS's own docs. And I'm starting to look into DayZ's approach now.

to do nothing — button grayed out, then reset, no server. Root-caused via direct SSH to the real VM:

- The container WAS actually running and had already booted successfully — `docker logs` showed
  `Listening on port 7777` / `Server started` well after the platform had already reported the job FAILED.
- `worker/game-control.ts`'s `GAME_POWER_PORT_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS` (30s) is too short for Terraria's real
  boot: world loading + "Settling liquids" (scales with world size), plus recovery time from a prior
  improper shutdown (`terraria.service`'s `ExecStop=docker stop -t 30` doesn't guarantee TShock's own
  console gets a clean `exit` — flagged separately below, not fixed here). The existing code comment
  claimed a slow family "only delays the SUCCESS notification, never falsely reports failure early" —
  that was incorrect; the timeout genuinely throws and fails the job.
- **Fix**: added `GameControlSpec.powerStartTimeoutMs` (optional per-family override, `lib/game-control.ts`),
  set to 180s for `terraria`, wired into `worker/game-control.ts`'s port-check call. Corrected the stale
  comment on the 30s default to describe what actually happens on timeout.
- Confirmed live: the customer's actual server is healthy right now (`docker ps` showed 3h uptime,
  logs confirm a clean listen on 7777) — the bug was purely the platform's own false-failure report, not
  data loss or a real crash.

**Not fixed here, flagged as a follow-up**: `terraria.service`'s stop path sends `docker stop` (SIGTERM),
which the `ryshe/terraria` image doesn't appear to translate into TShock's own graceful `exit` console
command — the container's logs show "TShock was improperly shut down" after a normal stop. AutoSave is
enabled so data-loss risk looks low, but a real fix (piping a clean `exit` into the console before the
stop signal, or confirming the image already handles SIGTERM correctly and this message is a red herring)
needs real verification against a live container, not assumed.

**Files:** `lib/game-control.ts`, `worker/game-control.ts`.

if [ "${GAME_UE5}" = true ]; then
  echo "Starting UE5 version"
  CONAN_BINARY=ConanSandbox/Binaries/Win64/ConanSandboxServer-Win64-Shipping.exe
fi

/etc/init.d/xvfb start
wine ${CONAN_BINARY} --userdir="${GAME_INSTANCE_NAME}" "${SERVER_NAME_PARAM}" "${SERVER_PASSWORD_PARAM}" \
    "${SERVER_ADDITIONAL_PARAMETER}" -nosteamclient -game -server -log &
WINE_PID=$!

sleep 10
tail -f "${CONFIG_DIR}/Saved/Logs/ConanSandbox.log" &

wait "$WINE_PID"
### Unreal Engine 5 update

With the new UE5 version of the game, the executable ``ConanSandboxServer.exe`` doesn't work anymore. A new ``GAME_UE5``
variable has been introduced, so that server admins can decide if they want to stay with the UE4 version of the game
or change to UE5.

**Note:** If you enable UE5, ensure you check the [Troubleshooting](https://exiles-enhanced.inflexion.io/servers/troubleshooting/) section regarding configuration file changes, as the engine migration may require manual adjustments to your `Engine.ini`.

### Environment variables

The only mandatory requirement is to pass the `GAME_INSTANCE_NAME` variable. Additionally, you can set some more
specific environment variables so that you don't need to touch the .ini files.

Based on the search results, here's what I found regarding loading .gma files on a Garry's Mod dedicated server:

Your server cannot use .gma files, so they must be unpackaged. This means that .gma files placed in the garrysmod/addons folder will not work directly without extraction.

The proper process requires:

1. **Extracting the .gma files**: You need to locate the gmad.exe file in your GarrysMod\bin\ directory and drag your .gma file onto gmad.exe to unpackage it into a folder with the same name.

2. **Installing extracted addons**: After extraction, upload or drag and drop the add-on folders inside the "addons" folder in /garrysmod/addons/ on the server.

Alternatively, for a more modern approach, dedicated servers can install addons straight from workshop collections by adding a startup parameter, and the server will download the collection at startup and mount all the downloaded addons.

So to directly answer your question: .gma files placed in the garrysmod/addons folder will not load without first being extracted using gmad.exe.

content.thinking:
My sed command seems to be inserting the DownloadManagers line after nearly every section header instead of just one, and I suspect it's a shell quoting issue where the escaped bracket pattern in my TS template literal isn't matching what I intended.

Found it — in a JS template literal, `\[` isn't a valid escape sequence so the backslash gets silently dropped, turning my intended regex anchor `/^\[IpDrv.TcpNetDriver\]/` into a bracket expression `/^[IpDrv.TcpNetDriver]/` that matches any line starting with those individual characters, explaining the many stray insertions. The fix is writing `\\[` in the Python string so it outputs `\[` literally in the TS file.

Since the test server's ini is now cluttered with junk lines but KF2 still boots fine, I'll leave cleanup for later and focus on getting the code right first. cat > /tmp/claude-0/-root/ec6fa978-d80b-4147-9982-eea470598e2c/scratchpad/mods/doc-entry.md <<'EOF'
## One-click mods for more game families — survey of all 52, 6 new families wired + live-verified, 2 new mod sources, Unturned fake-install fixed (2026-09-30)

Branch `feature/expand-mod-family-coverage` — **not merged, not promoted**: the owner reviews which families this turns on first. Owner's brief: real one-click mod installation for every family we sell, a new mod source wherever a game's real ecosystem lives, never a fabricated mechanism.

### Phase 1 — honest survey of every family not already wired

Before this pass 12 families installed for real (minecraft/rust/valheim by download-and-place; ark/unturned/dst/squad/soulmask/projectzomboid/tf2/l4d2/empyrion by Steam Workshop config-write). Terraria was out of scope (fixed in parallel on its own branch). Every other family was checked against the **production image's own source** (the live `OsTemplate.setupScript` was read from the prod DB, then each image's Dockerfile/entrypoint on GitHub), the game's own server docs, and the mod source's real API — with real requests, and for Steam Workshop a real anonymous `steamcmd workshop_download_item` run on a test VM (works for 602960, 544550, 1169040, 4000, 440900).

SURVEY_TABLE_PLACEHOLDER

### Phase 2 — what was built

`lib/mod-install-support.ts` gained **`FAMILY_SOURCES`**, a per-family allowlist of the sources the worker can really install for that family (the family-set + source-set pair alone would have drawn Install buttons for, e.g., Space Engineers' mod.io rows or Palworld's Nexus rows). Every pre-existing family is recorded with what it really does; Minecraft's two `github` rows lose their button — the generic GitHub adapter "installed" them by unzipping a release jar into a `plugins/nxeon-<slug>/` SUBFOLDER Paper never scans, a reported success with nothing loaded. Families not listed (Terraria, being worked on in parallel) keep the old behaviour. `familyInstallable` (NxLabs pages) now reads the family set instead of probing two hardcoded sources. Pure, unit-tested logic lives in the new `worker/game-mods-pure.ts` (`test/game-mods-coverage.test.ts`, 12 tests).

In `worker/game-mods.ts`:

- **Vintage Story** (`vintagestory_moddb`, 3,934 rows already catalogued) — the ModDB API (`/api/mod/{id}`, keyless) → the VM downloads the release zip from the ModDB CDN into `/opt/vintagestory/data/Mods` as `nxeon-<slug>.zip`. Release choice: exact game-version tag, else the newest release for the same major.minor (the game only enforces `game` as a minimum), never a different minor line — no match is an honest refusal. Dependencies come from each mod's own `modinfo.json` (read on the VM), missing ones are fetched from the ModDB as `nxeon-dep-<modid>.zip`. After the restart the fresh `server-main.log` is read to confirm the mod is in "Mods, sorted by dependency"; if the server restarted without it, that's reported as a failure. ModDB CDN links carry a raw space in `?dl=` — URLs go through the WHATWG parser before curl (caught live).
- **Satisfactory** (**new source `ficsit`** — ficsit.app, the Satisfactory Mod Repository; `scripts/import-ficsit-catalog.ts`) — public GraphQL + keyless downloads. Only versions with a `LinuxServer` build target are installable (Nxeon runs the Linux dedicated server); the full dependency closure (SML included — it's a mod like any other) is resolved against each dependency's semver condition and the server's own build changelist (read from `FactoryGame.log`), and nothing is downloaded until every piece has a compatible build. Each goes to `FactoryGame/Mods/<mod_reference>/`. Importer keeps only mods whose latest version ships a LinuxServer build (923 of 1,584; 373 excluded), downloads > 1000.
- **Arma Reforger** (**new source `reforger_workshop`** — Bohemia's own Reforger Workshop; `scripts/import-reforger-workshop-catalog.ts`) — the production image (`sknnr/arma-reforger-server`) writes `MODS_JSON_B64` into the server config's `game.mods` on every start, and the server downloads each modId (and its dependencies) from Bohemia itself. Always written, even `[]` — the entrypoint only touches `game.mods` when the variable is set, so clearing it would leave the last list in place. The Workshop has no documented API; its public pages server-render their data as `__NEXT_DATA__` JSON and robots.txt allows everything, so the importer reads the subscriber-sorted listing (198 addons ≥ 100 subscribers) plus each mod's own page for its real dependency count and license (95 of 198 have dependencies; 198/198 carry a license string). Nothing is downloaded by the importer.
- **Garry's Mod** (`steam_workshop`, appid 4000) — the item is fetched with the container's own steamcmd (anonymous), then **unpacked with `bin/gmad_linux`** (Facepunch's own tool, shipped in the server install) into `garrysmod/addons/nxw-<id>/`, and a managed `lua/autorun/server/nxeon_workshop.lua` calls `resource.AddWorkshop` for each so joining players fetch the same addon. Live testing corrected the first version: a packed `.gma` dropped into `addons/` is **not** mounted by a dedicated server (ULib/ULX placed that way never ran).
- **Necesse** (`steam_workshop`, appid 1169040) — container's own steamcmd → the item's `.jar` into `mods/` under the data dir (`/opt/necesse/mods`), which the server scans without any `-mod` argument (confirmed live — the entrypoint offers no way to pass one).
- **Killing Floor 2** (`steam_workshop`, appid 232090) — `ServerSubscribedWorkshopItems=<id>` lines under `[OnlineSubsystemSteamworks.KFWorkshopSteamworks]` in `LinuxServer-KFEngine.ini` (the server downloads each item itself), plus `DownloadManagers=OnlineSubsystemSteamworks.SteamWorkshopDownload` first under `[IpDrv.TcpNetDriver]` so clients can fetch them. Edited directly **with the server stopped**; the image's own `KF2_SERVER_SUBSCRIBED_WORKSHOP_ITEMS` env var was tried first and rejected on live evidence: its envini step only appends, so a removed id stayed subscribed and a kept one was listed twice.
- **Container recreate that reproduces the running container** (`inspectRunSpec` / `setContainerEnv`) — port bindings, bind mounts, stop timeout, hostname and any entrypoint/cmd override are read back with `docker inspect` rather than hand-copied into a per-family string; anything it can't faithfully reproduce is refused. `recreateContainer` (also used by the older ark/dst/squad/soulmask writers) now re-applies the 10m×3 json-file log cap every provisioned container gets — a recreated container used to lose it for good.
- **Mod downloads to a VM never carry a Nxeon credential.** mod.io's signed `binary_url` needs no key (checked live), the ModDB and ficsit.app are keyless, and Workshop/Bohemia downloads are done by the game or by Valve's steamcmd anonymously.

### Existing-family bug found and fixed: Unturned Workshop installs were fake

`applyUnturnedWorkshop` wrote `/opt/unturned/Servers/nxeon/WorkshopDownloadConfig.json` — correct only for fragsoc/unturned (Wave 2 seed). Production has run imperialplugins/unturned since Wave 7 (`-v /opt/unturned:/home/steam/Unturned/Servers -e SERVER_NAME='Nxeon Unturned'`), so that file was never read: **every Unturned Workshop install reported INSTALLED while the server ignored it**. The real folder can't even be derived from the env var — a live server named "Nxeon Unturned" created `/opt/unturned/Nxeon Unturned"` (trailing double quote, from the engine's own command-line quoting). The folder is now discovered (the one the server itself populated), the file is read-modify-written (the old code also clobbered the server's other settings), and a server that has never started gets an honest "start it once" instead of a guessed path. Verified live (below).

### Phase 3 — real verification against running servers

All on node-5, as the internal `e2e-test@nxeon.local` account, `isFree` (no billing). Vintage Story, Necesse and Garry's Mod were each a real production order of that family (the worker's normal PROVISION of the family's own setupScript). Satisfactory was a real Satisfactory order (16 GB tier); Arma Reforger, Killing Floor 2 and Unturned were then created on that same VM one at a time from each family's **exact** production setupScript run through `buildGameSetupScript()` (docker create + the generated systemd unit — only the `get.docker.com` prefix dropped), so the long installs didn't hold the production worker's serial job queue. Installs/removals were driven through the real `gameModSync` (DB-backed `ServerMod` rows on the test servers) or, where the catalogue rows exist only on staging (ficsit, Reforger), through the same exported apply functions with real ids.

Branch `feature/expand-mod-family-coverage` — **not merged, not promoted**: the owner reviews which families this turns on first. Owner's brief: real one-click mod installation for every family we sell, a new mod source wherever a game's real ecosystem lives, never a fabricated mechanism.

### Phase 1 — honest survey of every family not already wired

Before this pass 12 families installed for real (minecraft/rust/valheim by download-and-place; ark/unturned/dst/squad/soulmask/projectzomboid/tf2/l4d2/empyrion by Steam Workshop config-write). Terraria was out of scope (fixed in parallel on its own branch). Every other family was checked against the **production image's own source** (the live `OsTemplate.setupScript` was read from the prod DB, then each image's Dockerfile/entrypoint on GitHub), the game's own server docs, and the mod source's real API — with real requests, and for Steam Workshop a real anonymous `steamcmd workshop_download_item` run on a test VM (works for 602960, 544550, 1169040, 4000, 440900).

SURVEY_TABLE_PLACEHOLDER

### Phase 2 — what was built

`lib/mod-install-support.ts` gained **`FAMILY_SOURCES`**, a per-family allowlist of the sources the worker can really install for that family (the family-set + source-set pair alone would have drawn Install buttons for, e.g., Space Engineers' mod.io rows or Palworld's Nexus rows). Every pre-existing family is recorded with what it really does; Minecraft's two `github` rows lose their button — the generic GitHub adapter "installed" them by unzipping a release jar into a `plugins/nxeon-<slug>/` SUBFOLDER Paper never scans, a reported success with nothing loaded. Families not listed (Terraria, being worked on in parallel) keep the old behaviour. `familyInstallable` (NxLabs pages) now reads the family set instead of probing two hardcoded sources. Pure, unit-tested logic lives in the new `worker/game-mods-pure.ts` (`test/game-mods-coverage.test.ts`, 12 tests).

In `worker/game-mods.ts`:

- **Vintage Story** (`vintagestory_moddb`, 3,934 rows already catalogued) — the ModDB API (`/api/mod/{id}`, keyless) → the VM downloads the release zip from the ModDB CDN into `/opt/vintagestory/data/Mods` as `nxeon-<slug>.zip`. Release choice: exact game-version tag, else the newest release for the same major.minor (the game only enforces `game` as a minimum), never a different minor line — no match is an honest refusal. Dependencies come from each mod's own `modinfo.json` (read on the VM), missing ones are fetched from the ModDB as `nxeon-dep-<modid>.zip`. After the restart the fresh `server-main.log` is read to confirm the mod is in "Mods, sorted by dependency"; if the server restarted without it, that's reported as a failure. ModDB CDN links carry a raw space in `?dl=` — URLs go through the WHATWG parser before curl (caught live).
- **Satisfactory** (**new source `ficsit`** — ficsit.app, the Satisfactory Mod Repository; `scripts/import-ficsit-catalog.ts`) — public GraphQL + keyless downloads. Only versions with a `LinuxServer` build target are installable (Nxeon runs the Linux dedicated server); the full dependency closure (SML included — it's a mod like any other) is resolved against each dependency's semver condition and the server's own build changelist (read from `FactoryGame.log`), and nothing is downloaded until every piece has a compatible build. Each goes to `FactoryGame/Mods/<mod_reference>/`. Importer keeps only mods whose latest version ships a LinuxServer build (923 of 1,584; 373 excluded), downloads > 1000.
- **Arma Reforger** (**new source `reforger_workshop`** — Bohemia's own Reforger Workshop; `scripts/import-reforger-workshop-catalog.ts`) — the production image (`sknnr/arma-reforger-server`) writes `MODS_JSON_B64` into the server config's `game.mods` on every start, and the server downloads each modId (and its dependencies) from Bohemia itself. Always written, even `[]` — the entrypoint only touches `game.mods` when the variable is set, so clearing it would leave the last list in place. The Workshop has no documented API; its public pages server-render their data as `__NEXT_DATA__` JSON and robots.txt allows everything, so the importer reads the subscriber-sorted listing (198 addons ≥ 100 subscribers) plus each mod's own page for its real dependency count and license (95 of 198 have dependencies; 198/198 carry a license string). Nothing is downloaded by the importer.
- **Garry's Mod** (`steam_workshop`, appid 4000) — the item is fetched with the container's own steamcmd (anonymous), then **unpacked with `bin/gmad_linux`** (Facepunch's own tool, shipped in the server install) into `garrysmod/addons/nxw-<id>/`, and a managed `lua/autorun/server/nxeon_workshop.lua` calls `resource.AddWorkshop` for each so joining players fetch the same addon. Live testing corrected the first version: a packed `.gma` dropped into `addons/` is **not** mounted by a dedicated server (ULib/ULX placed that way never ran).

input.title: Restart after Minecraft/Rust/Valheim mod installs
input.tldr: The Mods panel tells customers that installing a mod restarts their game server. For Minecraft, Rust and Valheim the installer only drops the file in place and never restarts. The mod does nothing until someone restarts by hand. This session would add the restart and test it on real servers.
input.prompt:
Nxeon (repo /opt/nxeon — work in a git worktree off main, never build in /opt/nxeon; see CLAUDE.md). components/customer/gamepanel/v2/ModsPanel.tsx's banner says: "We fetch the file from its upstream source, drop it in the right folder for your loader, and restart the game service." But worker/game-mods.ts's installModReal/removeModReal (the modrinth/spigotmc/umod/thunderstore download-and-place path used by minecraft, rust and valheim) only place/remove the file and never restart — the mod stays inactive until the customer restarts manually (Rust/Oxide hot-loads .cs plugins, so Rust may be fine; Minecraft and Valheim/BepInEx are not). The families added on branch feature/expand-mod-family-coverage (2026-09-30) already restart via a `restartGame(conn, family, container)` helper in the same file.

Task: decide per family (owner-visible behaviour change: restarting kicks players) — either restart after a successful install/remove (reusing restartGame, batching so a multi-mod sync restarts once), or change the panel copy to say a restart is needed. ## One-click mods for more game families: report

**Branch:** `feature/expand-mod-family-coverage`, commit `4a82745f9f`, pushed to origin. It is **not merged into main and not promoted**, so the owner can review which families it turns on. The worktree is `/root/nxeon-worktrees/mod-coverage`. `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean and the new `test/game-mods-coverage.test.ts` passes 12/12.

### Phase 1: survey of every family not already wired
Every family was checked against three things: the production image's own source (I read the live `OsTemplate.setupScript` from the prod DB, then each image's Dockerfile and entrypoint), the game's own server docs, and the mod source's real API using live requests. For Steam Workshop I also ran a real anonymous `steamcmd workshop_download_item` on a test VM. It works for Barotrauma (602960), Stationeers (544550), Necesse (1169040), Garry's Mod (4000) and Conan (440900).

The 12 families that already worked were minecraft, rust, valheim, ark, unturned, dst, squad, soulmask, projectzomboid, tf2, l4d2 and empyrion. Unturned turned out to be broken and is fixed (see below). Terraria was left to the other agent.

| Family | What was found | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Vintage Story | Official ModDB API, no key needed; mods go in `data/Mods` | **Wired + live-verified** |
| Satisfactory | **New source ficsit.app**: public API, builds for Linux servers, SML mod loader | **Wired + live-verified** |
| Arma Reforger | **New source: Bohemia's own Reforger Workshop**. The image writes the mod list into the server config and the server downloads mods itself | **Wired + live-verified** |
| Garry's Mod | Workshop item, unpacked with the server's own `gmad_linux` | **Wired + live-verified** |
| Necesse | Workshop `.jar` placed in the data dir's `mods/` folder | **Wired + live-verified** |
| Killing Floor 2 | Workshop ids written into the server's ini; the server downloads them itself | **Wired + live-verified** |
| Conan | The image downloads the mods, then a `modlist.txt` activates them | Not wired: `modlist.txt` format unverified, and production may not boot at all (see issues) |
| Stationeers | `mods/` folder plus `modconfig.xml`, documented only by the community | Not wired, not live-tested |
| Space Engineers | Mod entries in two config files; the server downloads them itself. mod.io mods need crossplay mode | Not wired, not live-tested |
| DayZ | Needs the owning Steam account (Nxeon has one) to download, plus mod folders and signing keys | Not wired: DayZ has never been booted on this platform |
| Eco | mod.io game id 6 (confirmed with our key); download links need no key | Not wired: the mod archives use inconsistent layouts |
| Sons of the Forest, Sunkenland, V Rising | BepInEx mod loader running under Wine | Not wired: the Wine loading step wasn't tested, and the catalogue includes mod-manager apps and client-only tools |
| 7 Days to Die, Bedrock, CS 1.6 | Real mod folders exist | Not wired: no real catalogue source (CS 1.6's rows are mostly engine replacements, not plugins) |
| CS2 | One Workshop start map via an env var; plugins need Metamod | Not wired: CS2 is unsellable today (66 GiB install) |
| Factorio | The image already supports a mods folder | **Gated**: downloads need a factorio.com account token (tested: 403 without one) |
| Core Keeper | The image has its own mod.io installer | **Gated**: it wipes the mods folder on every start and only works if Nxeon's mod.io key sits in the customer-readable container env. Owner decision |
| ARK: Survival Ascended | One env var of CurseForge project ids; the server downloads them itself | **Gated**: building a real catalogue needs a CurseForge API key |
| Mordhau | Server downloads mod.io mods itself | **Gated**: needs a mod.io OAuth token (we only have an API key) |
| Insurgency: Sandstorm | Server downloads mod.io mods itself | **Gated**: needs a mod.io account email-code login, a security profile and an extra volume |
| Enshrouded, Dragonwilds | Community loaders / pak files | **Gated**: content is only on Nexus or CurseForge (both need keys) |
| The Isle | Workshop was shut down; pak mods circulate privately | **Gated**: no source to install from |
| Palworld | Official mods only work on the Windows server | **Gated**: owner decision on an unofficial third-party loader injected into the server process |
| Abiotic Factor, Icarus | Pak/loader mods scattered across GitHub | Not wired: no real catalogue (Abiotic Factor's official mod.io support isn't live yet; checked with our key) |
| Barotrauma | Mod mechanism works and anonymous downloads work | Not wired: the server itself can't be installed (see issues) |
| The Forest, Nightingale, ETS2/ATS | Nothing usable on the server side (Forest needs a Windows GUI tool; Nightingale's developer allows no mods; ETS2/ATS mods come from the player's own client) | **None** |
| Schedule I, Plutonium ×4 | Not orderable | N/A |

### Phase 2: what was built
- **A per-family source allowlist.** A family only offers one-click install for sources the worker really handles for it. This removes the buttons on Minecraft's 2 GitHub rows, which had been "installing" by unzipping a jar into a subfolder Paper never reads.
- **Six new installers** in `worker/game-mods.ts`, with the testable logic in the new `worker/game-mods-pure.ts`:
  - Vintage Story picks a release for the server's game version, pulls in dependencies listed in each mod's own manifest, and checks the server log afterwards to confirm the mod loaded.
  - Satisfactory resolves the full dependency chain, including SML, before downloading anything.
  - Garry's Mod, Necesse, KF2 and Arma Reforger as described in the table.
- **Container recreates now copy the running container's real settings** (ports, mounts, stop timeout) from `docker inspect` instead of a hand-maintained string. They also keep the 10 MB × 3 log cap that recreated containers used to lose.
- **Two new catalogue importers:** `scripts/import-ficsit-catalog.ts` (923 mods with Linux server builds) and `scripts/import-reforger-workshop-catalog.ts` (198 addons, with real dependency counts and licenses). Both ran twice on staging; the second run created nothing new. **Production doesn't have these rows yet.** Importing them is part of promoting the branch (`NXEON_DB_TARGET=nxeon … --apply`).

### Existing bug fixed: Unturned Workshop installs never worked
The installer wrote to `/opt/unturned/Servers/nxeon`, which only matches the old fragsoc image. Production runs imperialplugins/unturned, so every Unturned install reported INSTALLED while the server never read the file. The real folder can't even be derived from the server name: a live server named "Nxeon Unturned" created `Nxeon Unturned"` with a trailing quote. The installer now finds the folder the server itself created, edits the config file in place instead of overwriting it, and refuses honestly if the server has never started.

### Phase 3: what I checked on real running servers (node-5)
All test servers were owned by `e2e-test@nxeon.local`, free, and deleted afterwards through DELETE jobs; no orphaned rows remain.
- **Vintage Story, Necesse and Garry's Mod** were each a real production order of that game.
- **Satisfactory** was a real 16 GB order.
- **Arma Reforger, KF2 and Unturned** were then run one at a time on that Satisfactory VM, each from its exact production setup script, so their long installs wouldn't block the production job queue.

| Family | Test | Evidence from the server |
|---|---|---|
| Vintage Story | Installed Carry On, then Expanded Foods (which pulled in A Culinary Artillery); removed Carry On | The log listed the mods (`… carryon …`, `[Event] started 'CarryOn' mod`), then 6 mods, then 5 after removal. XSkills was correctly refused (no release for this game version). |
| Necesse | Installed and removed Increased Stack Size | `Found mod: Increased Stack Size (dianchia.increasedstacksize, 2.1.1) from ModsFolderModProvider`; 0 mods after removal. |
| Garry's Mod | ULib + ULX | They only ran after the fix: they created `data/ulib/groups.txt`, `data/ulx/config.txt` and more. My first version placed packed `.gma` files, which the server silently ignored. |
| Satisfactory (CL 502094) | BigNotes, then Refined Power with its 4 dependencies; removed Refined Power | `List of loaded mods: BigNotes, ModularUI, RefinedPower, RefinedRDApi, RefinedRDLib, SML 3.12.0` and SML's "Version check passed". Port 7777 was listening afterwards. |
| Arma Reforger | Where Am I + ACE Carrying, then an empty list | The server downloaded both itself, plus the ACECore dependency unasked; `Loaded addons` listed all three. With an empty list it loaded only the core game. |
| Killing Floor 2 | 3 items installed, 2 removed | `NetComeGo: Downloading item 1623217467`; after removal the next boot checked only `1130264785`. The image's own env var was tried first and rejected: it only adds entries, so a removed item stayed subscribed. |
| Unturned (fix) | M.E.I | `Successfully downloaded workshop item: 520546738 … Installed workshop item`. |

### Other issues found (not fixed; each has a task chip)
- **Barotrauma can't be provisioned at all.** Steam refuses the anonymous server install ("Missing configuration", reproduced twice). No customers are affected yet.
- **KF2's installed size is 30 GB**, which doesn't fit its 20 GB or 30 GB plans.
- **Conan may not boot.** The production setup script doesn't set `GAME_UE5=true`, which the image's README says is now required. I haven't tested this live.
- **Minecraft/Rust/Valheim mod installs never restart the server**, although the Mods panel tells customers they do.
- Necesse's 8 GB plan was 91% full right after provisioning.

Two more chips cover the next batch of families and the restart gap above.

### Things you should know
- My test provisions held the production worker's one-at-a-time job queue for roughly 45 minutes in total. Most of that was the failing Barotrauma order retrying 3 times. The permission system blocked a prod DB write to stop those retries, and I didn't try another way.
- I did not run `npm run build`. The worktree shares production's `node_modules`, and building in a shared tree has broken production before.
- I did not run `scripts/publish-docs.mjs`, because it would publish docs for unmerged code to the live docs page. Run it after merge.
- `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` (2026-09-30 entry, with the full survey table) and `ROADMAP.md` are updated on the branch.
- The temporary test harness scripts were moved out of the repo to `/tmp/claude-0/-root/ec6fa978-d80b-4147-9982-eea470598e2c/scratchpad/mods/harness/`.

Main files:
- `/root/nxeon-worktrees/mod-coverage/worker/game-mods.ts`
- `/root/nxeon-worktrees/mod-coverage/worker/game-mods-pure.ts`
- `/root/nxeon-worktrees/mod-coverage/lib/mod-install-support.ts`
- `/root/nxeon-worktrees/mod-coverage/scripts/import-ficsit-catalog.ts`
- `/root/nxeon-worktrees/mod-coverage/scripts/import-reforger-workshop-catalog.ts`

content.text:
I've sent the full report to the parent session. Six more games now get one-click mods, each checked on a real running server. The work is on branch `feature/expand-mod-family-coverage`, pushed but not merged or promoted, so the owner can choose which games to turn on.

**Newly wired, each confirmed from the running server's own logs or files:**
- **Vintage Story:** mods come from the game's official mod site. The right release for the server's game version is picked, and any mods it depends on are added automatically.
- **Satisfactory:** new mod source, ficsit.app (the game's community mod site). It pulls in the SML mod loader and any other mods a mod depends on.
- **Arma Reforger:** new mod source, Bohemia's own Reforger Workshop. The server downloads the mods, and any they depend on, by itself.
- **Garry's Mod, Necesse and Killing Floor 2:** all through Steam Workshop.

**Also fixed:** Unturned mod installs had never worked. They reported "installed" but wrote to a folder the server never reads. They now go to the server's real folder, and I confirmed a real download on a live server.

**Survey of the remaining families:**
- **Mechanism exists, not built yet:** Conan, Stationeers, Space Engineers, DayZ, Eco, and three games that use the BepInEx mod loader.
- **Blocked on a credential or an owner decision:** Factorio, Core Keeper, ARK: Survival Ascended, Mordhau, Sandstorm and Palworld. Each one's blocker is written up in `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md`.
- **No server-side mechanism at all:** The Forest, Nightingale, and ETS2/ATS.

**Problems found along the way (each has a follow-up task chip):**
- Barotrauma servers can't be set up at all right now, because Steam refuses the server download. No customers have one yet.
- Killing Floor 2 takes 30 GB once installed, which doesn't fit its 20 GB or 30 GB plans.
- Conan servers may not start: the image now needs a `GAME_UE5=true` setting that our setup script doesn't pass. I haven't tested this live.
- Minecraft, Rust and Valheim mod installs never restart the server, although the Mods panel tells customers they do.

**Before this can ship:**
- The mod catalogues for Satisfactory (923 mods) and Arma Reforger (198 addons) are on staging only. Production needs the two importers run as part of promoting.
- I didn't run `npm run build`, because the worktree shares production's installed packages and building there has broken production before.
- I didn't publish the docs page, since it would describe unmerged code as live.

**Impact on production while testing:**
- My test servers blocked the production job queue for about 45 minutes in total, mostly a Barotrauma test order that failed and retried three times. The permission system stopped me from cancelling those retries in the database, and I didn't find another way around it.
- All test servers were free, owned by the internal test account, and have been deleted.
